# Phase E3: exported plans and the box as a graph host - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for
> tracking.

**Goal:** A graph runs on the Pico box. The desktop plans a document for the RP2350 and exports it as a versioned,
checksummed blob; the firmware embeds the blob at build time and, at boot, loads it into a static arena with a portable
loader and runs it with the same executor the desktop runs, one block per main-loop pass. The box's bridge becomes that
built-in plan (`rp.device.midi-in` into a new portable `rp.core.midi-filter` into `rp.n8.nes`) in place of hand-written
forwarding, behind a generic box host with no N8 in it, and the box still does everything E2's gate recorded, at E2's
latency. `rp-device-check` loads and runs a 10-node plan through the same loader on a 4 KB stack. Every desktop suite
is bit-identical; the goldens that change on purpose are the `[packages]` golden (`rp.core.midi-filter` in every
product), the filter's new descriptor golden and three new blob goldens; nothing is re-recorded.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md), whose section 12 ("As
built") records the build and which Task 5 lands, sections 1 to 10 corrected in place. Task 1 writes the blob format
(`PlanBlob.hpp`), the loader (`PlanLoader`, portable, in `retroplug-graph-exec`), the exporter (`PlanExport`, desktop)
and its build-time tool `retroplug-export-plan`, with `retroplug_device_mode_objects` hoisted into
`cmake/packages.cmake` so the tool and the device-mode test share the device's builds of the packages; Task 2 adds
`rp.core.midi-filter` with the queue capacity `{"match": "<input>"}` it needs, and `packages/device-io`'s
`rp.device.midi-in` over the new `rp.device.midi-in/1` interface; Task 3 makes the box a graph host (`pico/host/`: the
block driver, the MIDI staging, the device host, the built-in plan, the UART path; `pico/n8-host/`: the box cart link,
its stats and volume write, `plan.json` exported at build time), with `-Werror=stack-usage=1024`, no heap reservation,
and the image run from SRAM; Task 4 puts the loader into `rp-device-check` with a plan of its own, a test package
(`packages/devtest`), the exporter's `--packages`, a judged pass line and a 4 KB guarded stack; Task 5 lands the docs.

**Tech stack:** C++20 (desktop GCC 13.3; the devcontainer's `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1 with newlib and its
libstdc++), CMake (`file(GENERATE)` registrations and custom commands that run the exporter at build time), the Pico SDK
2.1.1 with TinyUSB 0.18.0 and Pico-PIO-USB at `5a37a66`, Catch2, the TypeScript mock tier and `test-native`, pnpm
workspaces for the two new members. No submodule moves. **No implementer touches the hardware**: the Pico gate and the
one flash of `rp-device-check` are the controller's, in Task 6.

**Spec:** [modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md). The main design's Phase E outline is
[modular-graph-design.md](modular-graph-design.md) section 8; E1's design, whose device build the loader and the box
use, is [modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md); E2's design, whose gate E3 is held to, is
[modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md) (section 13.7), and E2's plan, the previous one
executed this way, is [modular-graph-phase-e2-plan.md](modular-graph-phase-e2-plan.md).

**Provenance:** every code block below was built and run before this plan was written, on the scratch branch
`proto/e3-host` in this worktree, on top of the design commit de026eb21: five commits, one per task (Task 6 is the
acceptance run and commits nothing), with GCC 13.3 on linux-x64 (a Ryzen 9 9950X, 32 threads). A block that creates a
file is that file as the prototype commit left it; one that changes it is the prototype's diff for it, so `git apply`
it from the step's text (or apply it hunk by hunk with the Edit tool). E3 moves and deletes no file. Each code task's
verification is the stage's last full run of `/tmp/e3pro/tip-verify.sh` with the legs its review fix passes ran again
(each task's suites step says which run each figure is from); Task 4's is the final verification
(`/tmp/e3pro/fin-*.log`), run at the prototype's tip, whose code is Task 4's, since Task 5 is docs alone. Every
expected pass, test count and figure is quoted from the stage reports in /tmp/e3pro, the latency report, those logs,
the design's record or the hardware gate's logs and record, which is what the generator checks; a figure no log records
is said to be so, and the step asks for it. When this plan was generated it was replayed in a scratch clone of
de026eb21, every block written or applied in order, and each task committed with the command given: each commit's tree
came out exactly as the prototype's, and each commit message as its. The prototype commits, by task:

- Task 1 `abf23e7d2`: the plan blob, exportPlan and the loader, proven on the desktop.
- Task 2 `07e511362`: rp.core.midi-filter and rp.device.midi-in, the box plan's first two nodes.
- Task 3 `51d8cc23a`: the box as a graph host, its bridge a built-in plan.
- Task 4 `d5b0a62bb`: rp-device-check runs a plan through the loader, on a 4 KB stack.
- Task 5 `0c788254b`: the docs. Task 6 is the acceptance run and commits nothing.

**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (de026eb21).** The design was written before the prototype;
this plan follows what was built, and Task 5 lands the design with section 12's record and sections 1 to 10 corrected
in place. In short:

- **The user's decisions** (`.superpowers/e-pico/decisions.md`, the E3 entries; design section 2): plans are built
  in only (exported by a desktop tool at the firmware's build and embedded; no SD plan file, no live upload); one
  block per main-loop pass sized by elapsed time, behind a block-driver seam a fixed audio cadence replaces later,
  and the Pico will process audio later, so the blob states its sample rate and `maxFrames` and the cart link only
  queues; defaults mean the same on every target, and the box's loader sizes the plan against a static arena and
  refuses, naming the node and the overrun, with the exporter running the same sizing so a plan that cannot fit
  fails the firmware's build; the firmware is a generic host that filters nothing (it still consumes its own `F0 7D
  50` commands), cart policy living in the plan through `rp.core.midi-filter`, `rp.n8.nes` cart-agnostic; the box
  link applies the node's expansion volume as N8Host does, retiring the box's mapper check. At the gate the user
  chose to find and fix E3's added latency before the plan, and **left every remaining decision to the controller's
  judgement overnight**; the controller's are marked as such below.
- **The design's decisions as built** (the design keeps the user's words and adds an *As built* note to three): no
  rule names `rp.core.delay`'s one-second default; a plan holding it alone needs about 396 KB, which the box's 128
  KiB arena refuses at export and at boot, and which `rp-device-check`'s 400 KiB arena holds (its per-type check
  runs it). BlipToaster's plan drops system common and real time too. Today's latency holds because the image runs
  from SRAM.
- **Alignment is the target's.** `max_align_t` is 16 on x86-64 and 8 on the M33, so every desktop device-mode type
  asked 16 and a type truly needing 16 was invisible. `PlanBlob.hpp` gains `kTargetAlign` (8, the rp2350's) and
  `node-sdk` `kDeviceAlign` (8), to which `node_device.hpp` aligns a device-mode instance and its tail on every
  compiler (a `static_assert` holds it to the Arm build's `max_align_t`); the loader and the exporter refuse more
  (`node-memory`), and the arena is aligned to `kBaseAlign`. The design's "16-byte `max_align_t`" reason for the
  estimate's safety no longer holds as written; every size and alignment being at least the device's does.
- **The blob, as built.** Every record is 32-bit words: a 17-entry section table, Strings, Settings (msgpack),
  Nodes, Steps, Views, ParamViews `{stream, wired}` (a param a wire drives is flagged, and `LoadedPlan::param`
  answers null for it, as the desktop's `setParam` refuses one), Channels, Queues, Streams, Clears, Rolls, Feedback,
  Masks, MaskBytes, Peers, PeerNodes, ParamStarts, then a CRC-32. The loader lays the plan out and sizes it in one
  pass (a bump that counts or places), so the measure and the placement cannot disagree; its codes are named
  (`plan-format`, `plan-version`, `plan-truncated`, `plan-crc`, `plan-target`, `plan-malformed`, `unknown-type`,
  `settings-invalid`, `node-memory`, `arena`, `create-failed`, `activate-failed`, `link-without-step`,
  `peers-without-link`).
- **The trial load and the estimate.** After sizing, `exportPlan` loads the blob it made into a host buffer of
  exactly the measured size over the device-mode builds and unloads it, so a create or activate only a device build
  refuses fails the export, and with it the firmware's build. The tool's `--header` form also writes
  `<symbol>ArenaEstimate`, the export's measured size, an upper bound on the device's (design section 12.5, question
  1): `rp-device-check` fails a plan that loads into more (the rig: 54,360 bytes against 56,064; the box's bridge
  29,976 against 30,560).
- **The blob is trusted.** The loader's checks bound its own reads and writes and catch corruption, but a device
  build has no `layout_for`, so they cannot hold a step's views to its node's layout. That holds while the only blob
  is the firmware's own build output; a live upload, left beyond E3, needs per-step port checks or a signature.
- **`capacity.match`.** The design's "whose capacity follows the input's" named no mechanism, and nothing had one: a
  queue capacity may now be `{"match": "<input>"}` (`rp::events_out::matching<"in">`, `defineNode`'s `{ match }`),
  exclusive with a size, naming an input of the output's own kind, resolved per plan by the planner's `capacities()`
  pass (a feedback wire's source too; an unwired input gives the default; a loop is refused, `capacity-match`). A
  fixed capacity could not serve both the box (256 / 4 KB) and the desktop (2048 / 64 KB). So the filter never
  drops, and the blob carries resolved sizes. `reserveMessage` (`graph/Queue.hpp`) holds a size to the room left
  instead of a sum, which a length near `UINT32_MAX` from `rp.device.midi-in` would wrap on a 32-bit device; every
  desktop decision is the one the sum made. `rp.host.midi-in` is one per document by the engine's type-id check, not
  `unique` as the design's premise had it, and refuses to activate without its interface; `rp.device.midi-in` is
  `unique` and activates with none.
- **`device-io` joins the device check's list in Task 2**, not Task 4: the device-mode test's `[device-check]` case
  requires every manifest `device` entry to be on it.
- **The box as built** (design section 5): `plan.json` drops `systemCommon` and `realtime` as well as the two
  aftertouches, since the old firmware forwarded channel voice and SysEx only and stress.sh's runstat case needs it;
  the staging stages every message whole with its status byte, a SysEx whole at its F7 (timed from it), and a byte
  the staging cannot hold stays in the UART ring (nothing lost to the bound); **the host ends each block itself**
  (`MidiStaging::endBlock` drops what the block did not take, counted as `untaken`), so a silenced
  `rp.device.midi-in`, a plan without one or no plan never jams the box's own commands; the **carry is bounded** at
  four blocks (21.3 ms), the excess dropped and counted (`skipped`), where the design's "a few blocks" was in fact
  thousands; `filtered = handed + tooLong + untaken - (pushes the link received - the node's own note-offs)`, the
  link keeping a mirror of `rp.n8.nes`'s note books (`made`) from its own answers, since the design's "staged minus
  received" miscounts the note-offs the node owes after a disconnect; `[stats]` gains `linkfull=` and `skipped=`.
  **The volume rule:** the link writes the node's value at every connect and on a change, and only a write the
  transport failed is retried, a second later (`CartVolume`); the link's -1 (N8Host's AUTO) writes nothing, so the
  register is 128 on every game where E2's gate read 129 and 139; the retry line says "did not go through", never
  `FAILED`, which the gate's `--fail` pattern matches. **After a power cut** under a live stream (`stress.sh`'s
  recovery case, `faults.sh`) a freshly booted ROM receives a few note-offs (`8c nn 00`) before anything else, paid
  by `rp.n8.nes` for the notes it held: E2's box sent none.
- **The image.** `PICO_HEAP_SIZE=0` is on the box only (`rp-device-check` keeps the SDK's 2 KB `.heap`);
  `-Werror=stack-usage=1024` (`cmake/device-image.cmake`, now included before the packages) is on every `device:
  true` library a device project builds and both images, Release and Debug, not on the desktop's `-device` objects;
  `loadPlan`'s no-error fallback, the one frame past it, moves into a never-inlined helper (`RP_NOINLINE`,
  `graph/noinline.hpp`, shared with the box host and the N8 pack's `Ops`); `rp.n8.nes` and the box link share one
  note rule (`rp::n8::noteEvent`); `pico/midi-in/midi.c` is cleaned to compile under `/W4 /WX` (behaviour
  unchanged); a constant-initialised static with any non-zero member lands in `.data`, so the staging and the link
  keep their state in all-zero structs in `.bss`. The arena is 128 KiB.
- **`copy_to_ram`, the controller's call overnight.** The first gate measured the flash-run image about 95 us later
  on average and 130 us at the worst than E2's (and one run had a 12.6 ms stall). The latency work counted the cause
  in an emulator and confirmed it on the rig with a trace build: a message's path is about six times E2's and fell
  out of the 16 KB XIP cache between messages (about four fifths of the cost was flash refills). The box image now
  runs from SRAM (`pico_set_binary_type(n8_host copy_to_ram)`, both USB variants), giving E2's latency back at the
  cost of SRAM (the RAM the image takes in all goes from about 200 KiB to 305 KiB of the 512 KiB, its code now among
  it); a non-blocking ring console that removed the stall was measured and dropped (+~100 us at the worst of every
  message), and the stall itself, a message arriving during the blocking `[stats]` print, is E2's hazard too and
  stays recorded, not fixed. `-DN8_LAT_TRACE=1` keeps the trace as an off-by-default diagnostic (`LatTrace.hpp`);
  its committed arithmetic has run only in the emulator. `tools/build-box.sh`'s size line says how much of the flash
  runs from RAM, where the load image ends and the RAM in all.
- **`rp-device-check` on the loader** (Task 4). The coupled pair, the signal and the digest come from a new
  workspace package, `packages/devtest` (`rp.devtest.plan`, `device: true`), listed by no product, so test nodes
  ship nowhere and the `[packages]` golden holds; they moved there from the device-mode test. `retroplug-export-plan
  --packages <name>,...` registers only an image's own packages (`N8_HOST_PACKAGES`, `RP_DEVICE_CHECK_PACKAGES`), so
  a plan naming a type the image lacks fails its firmware's build rather than its boot. **The plan check is
  judged**: `PlanStep` names a failing step (load, move, process, result, estimate, case), and a pass needs every
  move pushed, no drop, a digest node that heard sound and counted every block, and the loaded size within the
  estimate; the digest's value is float arithmetic and is not judged on the device, and the test compares the
  desktop's literal (`kPlanDesktopDigest`) only on `linux-x64-gnu13`. `rp.devtest.flood` and `rp.devtest.miscount`
  (in the test's `PlanNodes.hpp`) drive the remaining Result branches. **The stack guard:** `PICO_STACK_SIZE=0x1000`
  with `PICO_USE_STACK_GUARDS=1`, which writes the M33's `MSPLIM`, so an overrun faults (CFSR STKOF) instead of
  running into SCRATCH_X; the image links no `pico_multicore`, so it has no core 1 stack; it paints its stack and
  prints the high-water mark (the rig: 2,688 of 4,096 bytes).
- **The gates.** The first gate, on the flash-run image (normalised sha256 `b36bf92f...`), passed every leg but
  latency (742/1248, 1023/12589, 699/1198, 689/1223 and 700/1192 us average/worst against E2's 558-653 / 1083-1097
  on the same rig) and `faults.sh`, which gave 7 of 8 twice, each failure the plug's short-off quirk. The second, on
  the final image (`ffadfb26...`, `copy_to_ram`, the same bytes at Task 3's commit), passed: the boot 5.2 s after
  console start (E2 5.3 s) with `plan loaded: 3 nodes, 29976 of 131072 arena bytes` and the volume written;
  `stress.sh` 34 ok with latency 640/1086, 677/1114, 680/1098, 679/1128 and 610/1104 and no stall; A4 and C5
  identical to E2's; `faults.sh --rounds 8` 8 of 8 (after two attempts that never started: the Zigbee plug's short
  off left the N8 menu stuck at the first boot, the documented quirk); the upload and SysEx pick in 4922 and 4930
  ms. `rp-device-check` (`e14a1849...`) flashed once: 20 types, the N8 protocol, the plan in 54,360 of 409,600 arena
  bytes in 467 blocks with 8 moves and 0 drops, its digest `46e21691d4d54687` against the desktop's
  `b8854b2cc247318f` (they differ: FMA contraction), the stack at 2,688 of 4,096; then the box was flashed back.
- **The counts, start to end:** `retroplug-device-mode-test` from the baseline's 11 cases (2446 assertions) to 16
  (2872), 21 (3142), 40 (4220) and 43 (4386) over Tasks 1 to 4; `retroplug-graph-test` from 282 cases (356435) to
  295 (356647) at Task 2; `pnpm test`'s `define-node` from 20 cases to 21 at Task 2, its 174 files unchanged;
  engine-graph, parity, `test:native`, `test:ui`, `test:n8` and the render and kit legs unchanged; `device:check`'s
  image from 82528 / 2000 / 416402 (flash / data / bss) to 86858 (Task 2), 86870 (Task 3) and 130232 / 2000 / 416830
  (Task 4); the box from 48796 / 15324 / 32360 (PIO-USB) and 48756 / 1560 / 26128 (`RP_NATIVE_USB`) to 101200 /
  23832 / 188020 and 101576 / 9836 / 181788 (Task 3), of which 100628 and 101004 run from RAM.
- **Owed, not runnable here.** Windows, macOS and CI's arm64 Linux job have never built E3. The new libraries are
  ours, so they build under `/W4 /WX` on MSVC (`retroplug-graph-exec-device`, the exporter and its device objects,
  `retroplug-box-usb-cdc`, the device-io and devtest nodes), the three blob goldens' first run on another host is
  where question 5 (byte stability across hosts) is answered, so a red there is that answer rather than a
  regression, and a Windows export may accept a `long double` type Linux refuses (MSVC's is 8 bytes), harmless
  today. `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`, pull requests and pushes to `main` only, so a push of
  `feature/modularize` runs nothing: these runs are owed to a dispatched run or a PR the user (or their Windows
  agent) starts. The desktop N8 leg is owed to the user too: E3 changed the desktop's N8 path only by the shared
  note helper and `RP_NOINLINE` on `writeBattery`, which `[n8-node]`, `[n8-adapters]` and `test:n8` cover, and the
  leg needs the user to move the N8's USB cable. `RP_NATIVE_USB` has never run on hardware. Task 6 states all of
  them.
- **What no log backs.** No E3 stage ran the `env -i` CI dry run of `device:check` and `device:box`, the Reaper
  suite, `pnpm validate`, a fresh scratch configure, the CI views of parity alone and of `test:ui`, or the trace
  build from a fresh dir; Task 3 runs the last and Task 6 the rest, with E2's acceptance (`.superpowers/e2exec`) as
  the reference where the figure is unchanged and asks for the count where it is new. A task's intermediate state is
  never run: each task builds once all its files are placed. A few legs of Tasks 1 to 3 are quoted from the stage's
  last full run, before its fix passes, where those passes changed nothing the leg counts (Task 2's `reserveMessage`
  change, which every suite compiles, decides as the old sum did, and strict parity ran again after it); each suites
  step says which. The reds of Tasks 2 to 4 (Task 2's golden on Task 1's binary, Task 3's `[box],[usb-cdc]` on Task
  2's binary, Task 4's `--packages` on Task 3's exporter), Task 3's configure without the exporter and Task 4's runs
  of the exporter by hand are predicted from the code (no stage logged them). The gate's audio leg has no log of its
  own: its figures are the record's (`gate-commands.txt`, `results.md`). No parity baseline, kit golden, render
  baseline, descriptor golden of an existing type, `buildGraph` golden or `edio-golden.json` is re-recorded by any
  task. **The docs Task 5 lands say `skipped` is "0 expected outside a boot or recovery"** (the design's 12.7 table
  and the nes-hardware-lab skill; `pico/n8-host/README.md` makes no such claim), but the final gate's logs show it
  growing by a few hundred to about a thousand frames in every `stress.sh` run besides; `stress.sh` never judges it,
  and Task 6 asks for the growth to be reported. Correcting those docs is a follow-up after the plan, since Tasks 1
  to 5 must equal the prototype's trees.


**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**
- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 6 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own). No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with" trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code and of the specs): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself.
- Don't `rm -rf build` to fix CMake; investigate. Never use bare `git stash`, and never switch branches with uncommitted
  work in the tree. Never touch a submodule. `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (the two tracked
  patches): expected, leave it. `build-device/` and `build-box/` are scratch build dirs the device scripts own and
  `.gitignore` lists; removing them is fine. `pico/n8-host/build/` is the rig's build dir (ignored by
  `pico/.gitignore`); only Task 3's image step and Task 6 build there.
- The derived files are never committed: the embedded bundle C arrays (`build/native/*bundle_data.c`), the products'
  generated registration sources and providers headers (`build/packages/products/`), the device-mode objects'
  registrations (`build/device-mode/<target>-packages.cpp`, from Task 1) and `device-entries.cpp`, the exporter's
  package table (`build/export-plan/export-plan-packages.cpp`, Task 4), the device check's `DeviceCheckCases.hpp`, and
  the exported plans: the box's `n8_host_plan.hpp` (Task 3, under each firmware build dir's `generated/`:
  `build-box/pio/`, `build-box/native/`, `pico/n8-host/build/`) and the check's `DeviceCheckPlan.hpp` (Task 4,
  `build/device-check/` for the test and `build-device/generated/` for the image).
- **Parity holds the engine's output to the bit, and no task re-records anything.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`,
  `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE` or
  `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE`: a golden that moves means the step is wrong. **The goldens that change on purpose are placed
  from this plan's text**: Task 2's `[packages]` golden as a quoted diff (`rp.core.midi-filter` after
  `rp.core.buffer-recorder` in every row, each product's other ids and their order unchanged), and four NEW files,
  each quoted whole with its blob hash: the filter's descriptor golden (Task 2; `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE` is what
  records a descriptor golden) and the three blob goldens, `plan-blob.hex` (Task 1), `box-plan.hex` (Task 3) and
  `device-check-plan.hex` (Task 4) (`RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE=1` is what records a blob golden). They are not
  re-recordings: the prototype recorded each once, and this plan writes its bytes. The skip baseline
  (`packages/retroplug/scripts/skip-baseline.json`) does not change.
- **Run no `pnpm install` but the two frozen ones** (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, in Task 2 and Task 4),
  each right after the lockfile's diff and its new member's `package.json`. A non-frozen install re-resolves the
  lockfile: offline it silently prunes every other platform's optional packages (E2 lost 464 lines that way).
- Every whole-file block below (a `Create`) is followed by the `sed -n` range that extracts it from this plan and by the
  blob hash the file must have: write or extract the file, then `git hash-object <path>` must print the hash the step
  quotes, which is the prototype commit's blob. A retyped slip fails there rather than in a test that never reads the
  line. No new file is executable.
- Every `check:docs` count below is 83: the stages' logs record 82, and this plan is the 83rd tracked Markdown file
  `check-doc-links` walks. `docs/*-plan.md` are records: never edit one.
- The fixture groups need `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources` on the same command line; without it their
  cases skip. A shell `export` does not survive between commands. `pnpm test:native` takes ONE filter per run (an
  exact slug like `render-baseline`, or a dash-form prefix; `risa-render` runs its three files). The CI views pass
  `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/nonexistent-rp-resources RISA_SRC=/nonexistent-rp-risa`, because without them the runners
  fall back to `../resources`, which exists beside this worktree and holds some fixtures.
- The Catch2 binaries, `retroplug-render-host-test`, `rp-device-check-cases` and, from Task 1, `retroplug-export-plan`
  are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`: `cmake --build build` does not relink them, so a library edit needs the target built by name
  before a run (`pnpm test:plugin`, `test:n8` and `test:native` build theirs first, and the device-mode test depends on
  the exporter). `tools/build-box.sh` (Task 3 on) and `tools/build-device-check.sh` (Task 4 on) build the exporter in
  the desktop build themselves; `pico/n8-host/loop.sh` does not, and refuses to run without it. A new or removed source
  needs `cmake -S . -B build` first. The `-device` object libraries (the device-io and devtest nodes' among them) and
  `retroplug-graph-exec-device` (Task 1) are in the default build.
- The build trees were last built at the prototype's tip, so each task's first build in a tree re-runs CMake there and
  recompiles what changed; that is expected.
- The sanitizer trees are their own: `build-tsan/` and `build-asan/`. Configure one only if its `CMakeCache.txt` is
  missing (`cmake -S . -B build-tsan -DRETROPLUG_SANITIZE=thread`, or `build-asan` with `=address`); every task adds
  targets, so each task's sanitizer step re-runs `cmake -S . -B build-tsan` and `cmake -S . -B build-asan` first (the
  cache is kept). Build the binary in that tree before running it there; a stale prototype binary proves nothing.
- Case counts are exact. A `test cases: N | P passed | S skipped` line, an `All tests passed (A assertions in N test
  cases)` line and a per-file count must match the quoted N/P/S (Catch2 pads the `test cases:` line's columns with
  spaces, which the quotes below collapse to one). Assertion totals are exact for `retroplug-graph-test`,
  `retroplug-audio-test`, `retroplug-device-mode-test`, the launchpad, n8 and serial binaries and the small six.
  **A run of `retroplug-engine-graph-test` that includes `[engine-jobs]`, and so any whole engine-graph run and the
  sanitizer legs, reports an assertion total that moves from run to run** (its threaded cases): for those the case
  count must match and the total is the prototype's, quoted for scale.
- The prototype branch `proto/e3-host` is this plan's provenance, and no step reads it: every byte check is a blob
  hash or an image hash quoted in the step.
- The device steps need `arm-none-eabi-g++` (13.2.1 here). `pnpm device:check` uses `PICO_SDK_PATH` when it is set
  (this devcontainer sets `/opt/pico-sdk`, an SDK with no submodules, which is all the check needs); `pnpm device:box`
  needs the SDK's TinyUSB, so it uses `PICO_SDK_PATH` only when that carries it and `/workspaces/pico-sdk` (2.1.1,
  TinyUSB 0.18.0) otherwise, saying so, and Pico-PIO-USB from `PICO_PIO_USB_PATH` or `/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`
  (`5a37a66`, never edited). Both need a configured desktop build (`build/`), whose exporter they build. The CI dry
  runs clone both from GitHub.
- **No implementer touches the hardware.** Never open `/dev/ttyACM*` or `/dev/ttyDbgProbe`, never run
  `pico/n8-host/loop.sh`, `stress.sh` or `faults.sh`, never run `openocd` or `picotool`, never flash anything, and never
  touch the NES, the N8, the Pico, the Debug Probe, the L6, the video capture card or the power plug: the user's own
  sessions may be using them. The hardware steps of Task 6 are marked **for the controller**, who runs them under the
  nes-hardware-lab skill's rules.
- While a Reaper check runs it uses `build/bin`: do not rebuild the plugin until it finishes. Run one Reaper invocation
  at a time (`pnpm reaper:all`'s own fan-out is fine), with nothing else using Reaper or jackd meanwhile, and before
  each make sure no Reaper or jackd of an earlier run is left (`pgrep -a reaper; pgrep -a jackd`).
- Track progress outside the committed plan: never tick its checkboxes. Ticking one modifies
  `docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-plan.md`, and every task's expected `git status` list would then gain a line it does
  not show.
- The Windows build has not seen this tree (the prototype is local and Linux-only), so an MSVC-only warning is a real
  finding to report, not a stale quote; no step below builds on Windows, and Task 6 says what the owed Windows run is.
  macOS (AppleClang, libc++) and the arm64 Linux CI job have not run either: `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`,
  pull requests and pushes to `main` only, so their first run is a dispatched run or a PR the user starts, not a push
  of this branch.
- **When a step's result differs from its Expected, stop and report.** A different exit status, case count or quoted
  text is a finding, with three exceptions: an assertion total the rule above calls moving, a predicted failure whose
  failing file, case or target is the one named but whose wording differs, and a trap probe's quoted lines, whose
  object path and `(.text.startup.main+0x...)` offsets are this devcontainer's and this binutils': the device scripts

  its prototype commit, so a real defect found there is reported, not fixed; a fix belongs to a commit of its own after

### Task 1: the plan blob, exportPlan and the loader, proven on the desktop

Design section 4 and section 9's first commit. A plan for the RP2350 leaves the desktop as a versioned blob
(`graph/PlanBlob.hpp`): little-endian, 32-bit words, indices and offsets only, a header with the target, the sample
rate, `maxFrames` and the arena it was exported against, a 17-entry section table of fixed-size records and a CRC-32.
The records are what `PlanStorage` holds after planning, pool for pool, so the loader rebuilds a `PlanView` that
`runBlock` runs as it runs the desktop's. The loader (`graph/PlanLoader.hpp`, in `retroplug-graph-exec`, which the
device builds compile) checks the blob, lays the plan out and sizes it in one pass, refuses one over its arena naming
the node and the overrun, and runs it up in `PlanStorage::adopt`'s order, unwinding on a failure; it allocates and
throws nothing, and `retroplug-graph-exec-device` compiles it in device mode in the ordinary build. The exporter
(`graph/PlanExport.hpp`, desktop) plans a document for `Target::Pico` on a stub host, writes each node's settings from
its parsed settings, sizes the blob with the device's builds of the types and trial-loads it, so whatever the device
would refuse is refused at export. `retroplug-export-plan` is the build-time tool, with the device's builds beside it
through `retroplug_device_mode_objects`, hoisted out of `tests.cmake` so the device-mode test's objects use it too.

The device's alignment comes first (the host's device-mode builds now ask what the device asks), then the format and
the loader, the CMake function, the exporter and its tool, and the tests, whose blob golden is a new file. The tree is
built once, in Step 6: build nothing before it.

- Modify: `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/packages.cmake`, `packages/dsp/native/src/graph/nodes/DspNodes.cpp`, `packages/graph-runtime/native/CMakeLists.txt`, `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/graph/Packages.hpp`, `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`, `packages/native/cmake/warnings.cmake`, `packages/native/test/device-mode/DeviceModeEntries.hpp`, `packages/native/test/device-mode/DeviceModeNodes.cpp`, `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/PortTypes.hpp`, `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/node.hpp`, `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/node_device.hpp`

- [ ] **Step 1: The device's alignment, in `node-sdk`**

`PortTypes.hpp` gains `kDeviceAlign` (8, the RP2350's `alignof(std::max_align_t)`): `node_device.hpp` aligns a
device-mode instance and its tail memory to it in place of the compiler's `max_align_t`, so the desktop's device-mode
build of a type asks the alignment the device's asks (8, or the type's own when that is more), and a type that truly
needs 16 is seen at export; a `static_assert` holds it to the device's `max_align_t` on the Arm build only (the
RP2350's Hazard3 cores are riscv32, where it is 16). `node.hpp`'s `extra_memory` note says so, and `DspNodes.cpp`
asserts that the two kernels in tail memory need no more. On the device nothing changes: its images are the baseline's
bytes.

- [ ] **Step 2: The blob format and the loader**

`PlanBlob.hpp` is the format: the magic `RPPL`, version 1, the target (rp2350 = 1), the whole size, the sample rate as
two words, `maxFrames`, the arena, the pool sizes, the section table `{offset, count, recordBytes}` (the reader holds
each `recordBytes` to its own), the sections (Strings, Settings, Nodes, Steps, Views, ParamViews `{stream, wired}`,
Channels, Queues, Streams, Clears, Rolls, Feedback, Masks, MaskBytes, Peers, PeerNodes, ParamStarts) and a bitwise
CRC-32 (IEEE) of every byte before it; `kTargetAlign` (8) and `kBaseAlign`, the larger of it and `max_align_t`, which
the arena must be aligned to. `PlanLoader.{hpp,cpp}`: `sizePlan` (the count-only form), `loadPlan(blob, arena, types,
rp_host*, PlanLoadError*)` and `unloadPlan`; `LoadedPlan` holds the `PlanView`, the nodes (each with its fault flag
and drop counter), `find(id)`, `param(node, k)` (null for a param a wire drives) and `bytes`. The checks, in order:
magic, version, length, CRC, target, rate and `maxFrames`, the section table, every record's index and range, every
type id; then one layout pass that sizes and places (64-bit offsets with saturating products, everything placed
zeroed); then create and activate each node in document order, bind, check every peer list's `rp.link/1` before any
`set_peers`, `ports_changed`, the param starts, unwinding in reverse on a failure. The file has a paragraph on what it
trusts: the blob is the exporter's output for these builds of its types. `retroplug-graph-exec` takes the loader, and
`retroplug-graph-exec-device` compiles the executor and the loader with `RP_DEVICE`, no exceptions and no RTTI in the
desktop's default build; a device build takes the executor and the loader alone.

Create `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/graph/PlanBlob.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The exported plan's format (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 4): what the desktop's exportPlan writes
// (PlanExport.hpp) and a device's loadPlan reads (PlanLoader.hpp), the one definition both sides share. Portable: no
// heap, no exceptions, no standard container, so a device build includes it as the desktop's does.
//
// A blob is little-endian and 4-byte aligned, and holds no pointers: every reference is an index into a pool or an
// offset into a section. It is a header, a section table, the sections in the table's order and a CRC-32 of every byte
// before it. A section is an array of fixed-size records (or of bytes); the table gives each one's offset from the
// blob's start, its count and its record size, which the reader holds to its own so a writer of another layout is
// refused rather than misread (the version says which layout a writer meant; the record size catches one that lies).
//
// What a plan holds after the desktop planned it (PlanStorage.hpp) maps onto it pool for pool:
//
// - the nodes, in the document's order: id, type id and settings (msgpack, written from the instance's parsed
//   settings), its coupled group (the group's position in the schedule) and its step;
// - the steps, in the schedule's order: the node, the coupled group's size on its first member (0 elsewhere, and for
//   a node that is not coupled), and the step's input, output and param views as ranges of the view tables (each
//   param view saying whether a wire drives it);
// - the pools: audio buffers (each `maxFrames` floats, zeroed at load: the shared silence, the scratch every
//   unconnected output writes, every wire's buffer and each feedback front's channels), the channel table (which
//   buffer each entry of an audio view's channel array is), message queues by capacity (the empty one every
//   unconnected input reads, the scratch one every unconnected output writes, every wired output's and each events or
//   bytes feedback front's), control streams by capacity and start value (the empty one, every param's and control
//   output's, each control feedback front's) and resource cells (each a null handle at load);
// - after each block: the queues to clear, each with the node its drops are charged to, the streams to roll, the
//   feedback copies;
// - at load, after the nodes are created and activated, in PlanStorage::adopt's order: each linked node's peers, each
//   node's initial connected-output mask, and each param's start value from the document.
//
// Not carried: instance sizes (a device asks its own build of each type), resources (a plan that names one is refused
// at export) and settings commits (every device instance is created from its settings and never changes them).

#include <bit>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>

#include "graph/PortTypes.hpp"

namespace rp::graph::blob {

static_assert(std::endian::native == std::endian::little,
              "a plan blob is little-endian and is written and read as the host's own words");

inline constexpr std::uint8_t  kMagic[4] = {'R', 'P', 'P', 'L'};
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kVersion = 1;
// The targets a blob is exported for. The RP2350 is the only one; the field is there so a later target's blob is
// refused by name rather than run.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kTargetRp2350 = 1;
inline constexpr const char*   kTargetName = "rp2350";
// The most alignment a node instance may ask of an rp2350 arena: the device's max_align_t (graph::kDeviceAlign, which a
// device-mode build aligns its instances to). The loader refuses a type that asks more, on the device and in the
// exporter's sizing pass alike, so a type the device cannot place fails the firmware's build, not its boot.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kTargetAlign = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kDeviceAlign);
// "No node": a queue to clear whose drops are charged to nobody (the scratch queue unconnected outputs share).
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kNoNode = 0xFFFFFFFFu;

// The sections, in the order the table lists them and the blob holds them.
enum class Section : std::uint32_t {
    Strings,      // bytes: node ids and type ids
    Settings,     // bytes: each node's settings, msgpack
    Nodes,        // NodeRecord
    Steps,        // StepRecord
    Views,        // ViewRecord: every step's inputs then outputs
    ParamViews,   // ParamViewRecord
    Channels,     // u32: the buffer each channel-table entry is
    Queues,       // QueueRecord
    Streams,      // StreamRecord
    Clears,       // ClearRecord
    Rolls,        // u32: a stream rolled after each block
    Feedback,     // FeedbackRecord
    Masks,        // MaskRecord
    MaskBytes,    // bytes: the masks' connected flags, 0 or 1
    Peers,        // PeerRecord
    PeerNodes,    // u32: the node each peer entry is
    ParamStarts,  // ParamStartRecord
    Count
};
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kSectionCount = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(Section::Count);

struct SectionEntry {
    std::uint32_t offset;       // from the blob's first byte, a multiple of 4
    std::uint32_t count;        // records (bytes, for a byte section)
    std::uint32_t recordBytes;  // the size of one record: 1 for a byte section
};

struct Header {
    std::uint8_t  magic[4];
    std::uint32_t version;
    std::uint32_t target;        // kTarget*
    std::uint32_t size;          // the whole blob, its CRC included
    std::uint32_t sampleRate[2];  // the plan's sample rate, a double's bits, low word first
    std::uint32_t maxFrames;     // every audio buffer's length, and the longest block the plan runs
    std::uint32_t arenaBytes;    // the arena the exporter sized it against (0: none was given)
    std::uint32_t buffers;       // the audio buffer pool's size
    std::uint32_t cells;         // the resource cell pool's size
    std::uint32_t sectionCount;  // kSectionCount
    SectionEntry  sections[kSectionCount];
};

// A param as its node reads it: the stream, and whether a wire drives it (the stream is then the wire's source, a
// control output or a feedback front, which a host must not write: the desktop's setParam refuses a wired param).
struct ParamViewRecord {
    std::uint32_t stream;
    std::uint32_t wired;  // 0 or 1
};

// A run of a byte section: [offset, offset + size).
struct Bytes {
    std::uint32_t offset;
    std::uint32_t size;
};

struct NodeRecord {
    Bytes         id;        // Strings
    Bytes         type;      // Strings
    Bytes         settings;  // Settings
    std::uint32_t group;     // its coupled group's position in the schedule (a node not coupled is a group of one)
    std::uint32_t step;      // its step
};

struct StepRecord {
    std::uint32_t node;
    std::uint32_t groupSize;  // > 1 on the first member of a coupled group of that many consecutive steps, else 0
    std::uint32_t firstInput, inputCount;    // Views
    std::uint32_t firstOutput, outputCount;  // Views
    std::uint32_t firstParam, paramCount;    // ParamViews
};

// One port as its node sees it. `index` and `count` by kind (rp_port_kind): audio, a run of the channel table at
// `index`, `count` channels long; events and bytes, the queue `index`; control, the stream `index`; resource, the cell
// `index`; link, nothing.
struct ViewRecord {
    std::uint32_t kind;
    std::uint32_t index;
    std::uint32_t count;
};

struct QueueRecord {
    std::uint32_t messages;
    std::uint32_t bytes;
};

struct StreamRecord {
    std::uint32_t changes;   // its capacity
    std::uint32_t start[2];  // its value at load, a double's bits, low word first
};

struct ClearRecord {
    std::uint32_t queue;
    std::uint32_t node;  // whose drops what it drops are, or kNoNode
};

// A feedback wire's copy (Plan.hpp's FeedbackCopy). By kind: audio, `back` and `front` are runs of the channel table
// `channels` long, and `frames` is how many frames each front channel holds (at most maxFrames); events and bytes,
// queues; control, streams.
struct FeedbackRecord {
    std::uint32_t kind;
    std::uint32_t back;
    std::uint32_t front;
    std::uint32_t channels;
    std::uint32_t frames;
};

// A node's connected-output mask, `count` flags at `offset` in MaskBytes: count is the node's output count.
struct MaskRecord {
    std::uint32_t node;
    std::uint32_t offset;
    std::uint32_t count;
};

// A linked node's peers: `count` entries of PeerNodes from `first`.
struct PeerRecord {
    std::uint32_t node;
    std::uint32_t first;
    std::uint32_t count;
};

// A param's start value from the document: the stream starts there, its queued changes dropped (PlanStorage::adopt).
struct ParamStartRecord {
    std::uint32_t stream;
    std::uint32_t value[2];  // a double's bits, low word first
};

// The record size each section holds (1 for bytes).
constexpr std::uint32_t recordBytes(Section s) {
    switch (s) {
        case Section::Strings:
        case Section::Settings:
        case Section::MaskBytes: return 1;
        case Section::Nodes: return sizeof(NodeRecord);
        case Section::Steps: return sizeof(StepRecord);
        case Section::Views: return sizeof(ViewRecord);
        case Section::Queues: return sizeof(QueueRecord);
        case Section::Streams: return sizeof(StreamRecord);
        case Section::Clears: return sizeof(ClearRecord);
        case Section::Feedback: return sizeof(FeedbackRecord);
        case Section::Masks: return sizeof(MaskRecord);
        case Section::Peers: return sizeof(PeerRecord);
        case Section::ParamStarts: return sizeof(ParamStartRecord);
        case Section::ParamViews: return sizeof(ParamViewRecord);
        case Section::Channels:
        case Section::Rolls:
        case Section::PeerNodes:
        case Section::Count: break;
    }
    return sizeof(std::uint32_t);
}

// Every record is whole words, so a section of them keeps the blob 4-byte aligned; a byte section is padded to 4.
static_assert(sizeof(Header) % 4 == 0 && sizeof(NodeRecord) % 4 == 0 && sizeof(StepRecord) % 4 == 0 &&
              sizeof(ViewRecord) % 4 == 0 && sizeof(StreamRecord) % 4 == 0 && sizeof(FeedbackRecord) % 4 == 0 &&
              sizeof(ParamStartRecord) % 4 == 0);
static_assert(sizeof(Header) == 44 + 12 * kSectionCount, "the header is words, with no padding");

// A double as the two words a blob holds it in, and back.
inline void splitDouble(double v, std::uint32_t (&out)[2]) {
    const auto bits = std::bit_cast<std::uint64_t>(v);
    out[0] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(bits);
    out[1] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(bits >> 32);
}
inline double joinDouble(const std::uint32_t (&in)[2]) {
    return std::bit_cast<double>(std::uint64_t{in[0]} | (std::uint64_t{in[1]} << 32));
}

// CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, the reflected 0xEDB88320 polynomial, as zlib's crc32), bit by bit: a blob is read once, at load,
// so a table's kilobyte of flash buys nothing.
inline std::uint32_t crc32(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
    std::uint32_t crc = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) {
        crc ^= data[i];
        for (int k = 0; k < 8; ++k) crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xEDB88320u & (0u - (crc & 1u)));
    }
    return ~crc;
}

}  // namespace rp::graph::blob
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The loader (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 4): an exported plan (PlanBlob.hpp) laid out in an arena
// the caller owns, its nodes created and run up, and handed to the executor as a PlanView. Portable: it allocates
// nothing, throws nothing and reaches every node through the C ABI, so the device runs it as the desktop does; the
// desktop's exportPlan runs its sizing pass (sizePlan) over the blob it wrote, with the device's builds of the types,
// so a plan that would not fit is refused at export by the same arithmetic the device refuses it with.
//
// loadPlan, in order: checks the blob (its magic, its version, its length, its CRC, every index and offset in bounds,
// every type id registered), sizes it (each node's own query_memory on its settings, plus every pool, view array, step
// and counter) and refuses one over the arena, naming the node that tips it over and by how much, before it creates
// anything; then lays it out and runs it up in PlanStorage::adopt's order: create and activate each node in the
// document's order, bind the steps, tell each linked node its peers, each node its connected outputs, and start each
// param the document sets. A failure part-way unwinds what it made, in reverse, and names the node and the step.
// unloadPlan deactivates and destroys the nodes in reverse.
//
// The blob is read in place and must outlive the plan loaded from it (on the device it is in flash): node ids and the
// masks point into it. The arena must be aligned to the larger of the target's alignment (PlanBlob.hpp's kTargetAlign,
// the RP2350's max_align_t) and the compiler's max_align_t, and a node type that asks for more than the target's
// alignment is refused, on the desktop's sizing pass as on the device, so the sizing pass and the layout are one
// computation wherever they run.
//
// The blob is trusted to be the exporter's output for these builds of its types. The checks keep the loader's own
// reads and writes in bounds (every index, offset and count, overflow-safe) and refuse a corrupted blob (the CRC), but
// nothing here can hold a step's views to its node's layout: a device build of a type has no layout_for
// (node_device.hpp), and a node reads its inputs and outputs by its layout's ordinals without consulting the counts. A
// blob crafted with fewer views than a type has ports, or a queue where it has an audio port, would make that node
// read or write out of bounds. That holds while every plan a device runs is built into its firmware by the exporter
// (the E3 design's decision 1); a blob from outside the firmware (a plan file, a live upload) needs each step's port
// kinds and counts checked against something the device knows, or a signature.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <span>
#include <string_view>

#include "graph/Plan.hpp"
#include "graph/rp_node.h"

namespace rp::graph {

// Why a plan was refused: a code (the planner's where it has one: "unknown-type", "settings-invalid", "create-failed",
// "activate-failed", "link-without-step"; the loader's own: "plan-format", "plan-version", "plan-truncated",
// "plan-crc", "plan-target", "plan-malformed", "arena", "node-memory", "peers-without-link"), the node's id where one
// is at fault (cut to fit), and a sentence.
struct PlanLoadError {
    char code[32];
    char node[64];
    char message[256];
};

// What a plan needs of an arena: `bytes` in all, of which `instanceBytes` are its nodes' own instances.
struct PlanSize {
    std::size_t   bytes = 0;
    std::size_t   instanceBytes = 0;
    std::uint32_t nodes = 0;
};

// One node of a loaded plan. Its fault flag and drop counter are the executor's (PlanStep::faulted, OutputQueue::drops)
// and live here, in the arena.
struct LoadedNode {
    const char*                id = nullptr;  // into the blob, not NUL-terminated
    std::uint32_t              idSize = 0;
    const rp_node_type*        type = nullptr;
    rp_node*                   node = nullptr;
    void*                      memory = nullptr;
    std::size_t                memoryBytes = 0;
    std::uint32_t              step = 0;
    std::atomic<bool>          faulted{false};
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> drops{0};
    bool                       active = false;

    std::string_view name() const { return {id, idSize}; }
};

struct LoadedPlan {
    PlanView                   view;       // what runBlock runs
    double                     sampleRate = 0.0;
    std::uint32_t              maxFrames = 0;  // the longest block it takes
    std::span<LoadedNode>      nodes;      // in the document's order
    std::size_t                bytes = 0;  // what the plan takes of the arena it was laid out in
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> faults{0};  // nodes that have faulted
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> drops{0};   // messages full output queues have dropped

    // The node with this id, or null.
    LoadedNode* find(std::string_view id) const;
    // Node `n`'s param `k` (in its layout's order): its own control stream, which a host writes a change into before a
    // block (pushControl). Null for a param a wire drives (it reads the wire's source, another node's output, which the
    // desktop's setParam refuses to write), and past the node's params.
    rp_control_queue* param(std::uint32_t n, std::uint32_t k) const;

    rp_control_queue* const* paramViews = nullptr;  // every step's param views, in step order
    const std::uint8_t*      wired = nullptr;       // per param view: a wire drives it
};

// Checks the blob and sizes it against an arena of `arenaBytes` (0: any size), creating nothing; `types` are the
// packages whose node types it may name (a product's rp_register_packages()). False, with `error` filled, for a blob
// loadPlan would refuse before it created a node. `size` is filled once every node's query_memory has answered, so on
// a pass and on an over-budget refusal, not on a refused blob, settings or alignment, or sizes that overflow.
bool sizePlan(std::span<const std::uint8_t> blob, std::span<const rp_package* const> types, std::size_t arenaBytes,
              PlanSize* size, PlanLoadError* error);

// Loads the blob into `arena` (see above) with its nodes created under `host`. The plan, at the arena's start, or null
// with `error` filled and nothing left created.
LoadedPlan* loadPlan(std::span<const std::uint8_t> blob, std::span<std::byte> arena,
                     std::span<const rp_package* const> types, const rp_host* host, PlanLoadError* error);

// Deactivates and destroys every node, in reverse. The arena is the caller's again afterwards.
void unloadPlan(LoadedPlan* plan);

}  // namespace rp::graph
````
