`MidiFilter.test.cpp` (8 cases, `[graph][core][midi-filter]`): each kind dropped alone over a 17-message stream (tied
frames, flags, both SysEx forms, real-time bytes among channel messages, a data-led run, a velocity-0 note-on, a
two-message message), an empty list passing everything, the box plan's two aftertouches, the first-byte rule, the
matched capacity (680 messages on a 1024-message source pass whole where an `rp.core.merge` drops 424), nothing
allocated from the first block, the refusals and the descriptor golden. `QueueCapacity.test.cpp`: a chain of matches,
a feedback-wired one and the loop refusal, the matched budget's advice, and `reserveMessage` held to the room left at
a 32-bit wrap (`0xFFFFFFFDu` after 3 bytes). `Descriptor.test.cpp`: the match's parse, write and round trip, and each
refusal. `NoAlloc.test.cpp`'s every-`rp.core`-node document holds a filter. `define-node.test.ts` (20 cases to 21):
the TS parse of a match with the C++ refusal words and the union's `@ts-expect-error`.

Create `packages/native/test/graph/MidiFilter.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// rp.core.midi-filter (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 6): drops the MIDI messages of the kinds its
// `drop` names and passes every other one as it came, frame, flags, bytes and order, through a real plan.
//
// - A stream of every kind, a SysEx, a lone F7 and real-time messages among the channel messages, frames tied and
//   flags set: each kind dropped alone leaves exactly the rest, an empty list (and no settings at all) passes it whole,
//   and BlipToaster's list, the box plan's (both aftertouches), drops those two alone.
// - A kind is the first byte's: a message led by a data byte is of no kind and passes whatever is dropped (no running
//   status is kept across messages), a note-on with velocity 0 is a noteOn, and a message carrying two is its first's.
// - Its output is sized as whatever feeds its input (rp::events_out::matching<"in">), so a stream past the default
//   passes whole where a default-sized output drops; nothing is allocated once the plan runs; a kind named twice or
//   one that is no kind is refused as the settings.
// - Its descriptor is its golden (golden/rp.core.midi-filter.descriptor.json; RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1 records it).
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <fstream>
#include <initializer_list>
#include <iterator>
#include <sstream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "GraphRig.hpp"

using namespace rp::graph;
using rp::graph::test::GraphRig;

namespace {

struct Message {
    std::uint32_t                frame;
    std::uint32_t                flags;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t>    bytes;
    const char*                  kind;  // the filter's label for it, or "" for none
};

// Every kind once, and the edges: frames tied and in order, a flag on some, SysEx in both its forms, a message led by
// a data byte, a velocity-0 note-on, real-time bytes among channel messages, and a message holding two.
const std::vector<Message>& stream() {
    static const std::vector<Message> s = {
        {0, 0, {0x80, 60, 0}, "noteOff"},
        {0, 1, {0x91, 60, 100}, "noteOn"},
        {2, 0, {0xA2, 60, 10}, "polyAftertouch"},
        {2, 0, {0xF8}, "realtime"},
        {3, 0, {0xB3, 7, 100}, "controlChange"},
        {5, 1, {0xC4, 5}, "programChange"},
        {5, 0, {0xD5, 20}, "channelAftertouch"},
        {9, 0, {0xE6, 0, 64}, "pitchBend"},
        {9, 1, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x50, 0x01, 0xF7}, "sysex"},
        {12, 0, {0xF2, 0x10, 0x00}, "systemCommon"},
        {12, 0, {0xF7}, "sysex"},
        {13, 0, {0x40, 50}, ""},
        {20, 0, {0x90, 61, 0}, "noteOn"},
        {20, 0, {0xFA}, "realtime"},
        {21, 0, {0xF6}, "systemCommon"},
        {30, 0, {0xA0, 61, 3, 0x90, 62, 100}, "polyAftertouch"},
        {31, 0, {0xFF}, "realtime"},
    };
    return s;
}

const std::vector<std::string> kKinds = {"noteOff",           "noteOn",     "polyAftertouch", "controlChange",
                                         "programChange",     "channelAftertouch", "pitchBend", "sysex",
                                         "systemCommon",      "realtime"};

// The stream, `repeat` times a block, on an events output whose capacity its settings declare (0: the default).
struct ScriptSettings {
    std::uint32_t repeat = 1;
    std::uint32_t messages = 0;
};

struct Script {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.midi-script";
    using Settings = ScriptSettings;
    struct { rp::events_out out; } outputs;
    static void adjust_layout(Layout& l, const Settings& s) {
        if (s.messages) l.ports[0].capacity.messages = s.messages;
    }
    std::uint32_t repeat = 1;
    void on_settings(const Settings& s) noexcept { repeat = s.repeat; }
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        for (std::uint32_t r = 0; r < repeat; ++r)
            for (const Message& m : stream()) outputs.out.push(m.frame, m.bytes, m.flags);
    }
};

// What reached its input in the last block, and the queue it came on; reserved, so a block allocates nothing.
struct Seen {
    std::uint32_t                frame = 0;
    std::uint32_t                flags = 0;
    std::uint32_t                size = 0;
    std::array<std::uint8_t, 8>  bytes{};
};

struct Log {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.midi-log";
    struct { rp::events_in in; } inputs;
    std::vector<Seen> seen;
    std::uint32_t     count = 0;  // every message, kept or not
    std::uint32_t     capacity = 0, bytesCapacity = 0;
    Log() { seen.reserve(1024); }
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        seen.clear();
        count = 0;
        capacity = inputs.in.queue->capacity;
        bytesCapacity = inputs.in.queue->bytes_capacity;
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.in.messages()) {
            ++count;
            if (seen.size() == seen.capacity()) continue;
            Seen s;
            s.frame = m.frame;
            s.flags = m.flags;
            s.size = m.size;
            const auto data = inputs.in.data(m);
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < data.size() && i < s.bytes.size(); ++i) s.bytes[i] = data[i];
            seen.push_back(s);
        }
    }
};

const rp_package* filterTestPackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<Script>(), rp::node_type<Log>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.midi-filter"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

struct FilterRig : GraphRig {
    FilterRig() { registry.addPackage(filterTestPackage()); }
};

// The script through a filter of these settings (none: the node carries no "settings") into the log.
std::string doc(const std::string& filter, const std::string& script = "{}") {
    const std::string settings = filter.empty() ? "" : R"(,"settings":)" + filter;
    return R"({"nodes":[{"id":"s","type":"rp.test.midi-script","settings":)" + script +
           R"(},{"id":"f","type":"rp.core.midi-filter")" + settings + R"(},{"id":"log","type":"rp.test.midi-log"}],)"
           R"("wires":[{"from":"s.out","to":"f.in"},{"from":"f.out","to":"log.in"}]})";
}

std::string dropList(std::initializer_list<std::string> kinds) {
    std::string out = R"({"drop":[)";
    bool first = true;
    for (const auto& k : kinds) {
        out += (first ? "\"" : ",\"") + k + "\"";
        first = false;
    }
    return out + "]}";
}

// One line a message: frame, flags, bytes.
std::string line(std::uint32_t frame, std::uint32_t flags, const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t size) {
    std::ostringstream o;
    o << frame << " " << flags << ":";
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) o << " " << std::hex << static_cast<int>(bytes[i]) << std::dec;
    return o.str() + "\n";
}
std::string expected(const std::vector<std::string>& dropped) {
    std::string out;
    for (const Message& m : stream()) {
        bool drop = false;
        for (const auto& k : dropped) drop = drop || k == m.kind;
        if (!drop) out += line(m.frame, m.flags, m.bytes.data(), m.bytes.size());
    }
    return out;
}
std::string got(const Log& log) {
    std::string out;
    for (const Seen& s : log.seen) out += line(s.frame, s.flags, s.bytes.data(), s.size);
    return out;
}

// The golden's text, its line ending dropped as DspNodes.test.cpp drops it.
std::string readFile(const std::string& path) {
    std::ifstream     in(path);
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << in.rdbuf();
    std::string s = ss.str();
    while (!s.empty() && (s.back() == '\n' || s.back() == '\r')) s.pop_back();
    return s;
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("the MIDI filter drops each kind alone, and passes the rest as it came", "[graph][core][midi-filter]") {
    // Every kind the stream holds is one of the filter's, and each of the filter's is in it.
    for (const auto& k : kKinds) {
        bool held = false;
        for (const Message& m : stream()) held = held || k == m.kind;
        INFO(k);
        CHECK(held);
    }
    FilterRig rig;
    for (const auto& kind : kKinds) {
        INFO(kind);
        const SetGraphResult r = rig.set(doc(dropList({kind})));
        INFO(GraphRig::codes(r));
        REQUIRE(r.ok);
        rig.run();
        const Log& log = rig.node<Log>("log");
        CHECK(got(log) == expected({kind}));
        CHECK(log.count < stream().size());
        CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("an empty drop list, or none, passes every message, its frame, flags and order kept",
          "[graph][core][midi-filter]") {
    FilterRig rig;
    for (const std::string& settings : {std::string(), std::string("{}"), std::string(R"({"drop":[]})")}) {
        INFO(settings);
        REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(settings)).ok);
        rig.run(64, 2);
        const Log& log = rig.node<Log>("log");
        CHECK(log.count == stream().size());
        CHECK(got(log) == expected({}));
    }
}

TEST_CASE("the box plan's list drops both aftertouches from among channel, SysEx and real-time messages",
          "[graph][core][midi-filter]") {
    FilterRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(dropList({"polyAftertouch", "channelAftertouch"}))).ok);
    rig.run();
    const Log& log = rig.node<Log>("log");
    CHECK(got(log) == expected({"polyAftertouch", "channelAftertouch"}));
    // What is left still holds its SysEx, its real-time bytes and its channel messages, in their places.
    CHECK(log.count == stream().size() - 3);

    // Everything dropped: what is left is the one message of no kind, a run led by a data byte.
    std::string all = R"({"drop":[)";
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kKinds.size(); ++i) all += (i ? ",\"" : "\"") + kKinds[i] + "\"";
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(all + "]}")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(got(rig.node<Log>("log")) == "13 0: 40 32\n");
}

TEST_CASE("a message's kind is its first byte's", "[graph][core][midi-filter]") {
    FilterRig rig;
    // A velocity-0 note-on is a noteOn: dropping note-offs leaves it, dropping note-ons takes it.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(dropList({"noteOff"}))).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(got(rig.node<Log>("log")).find("20 0: 90 3d 0\n") != std::string::npos);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(dropList({"noteOn"}))).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(got(rig.node<Log>("log")).find("20 0: 90 3d 0\n") == std::string::npos);
    // A message holding a poly aftertouch then a note-on is a polyAftertouch, whole; a lone F7 is a sysex, and the
    // data-led run passes even with every channel kind dropped.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(dropList({"polyAftertouch", "sysex", "noteOff", "noteOn", "controlChange", "programChange",
                                  "channelAftertouch", "pitchBend"})))
                .ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(got(rig.node<Log>("log")) == expected({"polyAftertouch", "sysex", "noteOff", "noteOn", "controlChange",
                                                 "programChange", "channelAftertouch", "pitchBend"}));
    CHECK(got(rig.node<Log>("log")).find("30 0:") == std::string::npos);
    CHECK(got(rig.node<Log>("log")).find("12 0: f7") == std::string::npos);
    CHECK(got(rig.node<Log>("log")).find("13 0: 40 32\n") != std::string::npos);
}

TEST_CASE("the MIDI filter's output is sized as what feeds it, so a stream past the default passes whole",
          "[graph][core][midi-filter]") {
    FilterRig rig;
    // 40 copies of the stream, 680 messages and 1360 bytes, on a source that declares 1024 messages: the filter's
    // queue is the source's, and nothing is dropped anywhere.
    const std::uint32_t copies = 40;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc("{}", R"({"repeat":40,"messages":1024})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    const Log& log = rig.node<Log>("log");
    CHECK(log.capacity == 1024);
    CHECK(log.bytesCapacity == kDefaultQueueBytes);
    CHECK(log.count == copies * stream().size());
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);
    // Fed from a default-sized source, it is default-sized itself.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc("{}")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Log>("log").capacity == kDefaultQueueMessages);
    CHECK(rig.node<Log>("log").bytesCapacity == kDefaultQueueBytes);
    // Where an output of the default size would drop what passes 256, charged to that output's node.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"s","type":"rp.test.midi-script","settings":{"repeat":40,"messages":1024}},
                                  {"id":"m","type":"rp.core.merge","settings":{"inputs":1}},
                                  {"id":"log","type":"rp.test.midi-log"}],
                         "wires":[{"from":"s.out","to":"m.in1"},{"from":"m.out","to":"log.in"}]})")
                .ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Log>("log").count == kDefaultQueueMessages);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("m") == copies * stream().size() - kDefaultQueueMessages);
}

TEST_CASE("the MIDI filter allocates nothing once its plan runs", "[graph][core][midi-filter]") {
    FilterRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(dropList({"polyAftertouch", "realtime"}), R"({"repeat":8})")).ok);
    // The script's stream is a function-local static, made before the window (this case may run first).
    const std::size_t messages = stream().size();
    // Counted from the plan's first block.
    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations();
    rig.run(64, 6);
    const rp::test::AllocationCount m = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
    CHECK(m.allocations == 0);
    CHECK(m.frees == 0);
    CHECK(rig.node<Log>("log").count == 8 * (messages - 5));
}

TEST_CASE("the MIDI filter refuses a kind named twice, or one that is no kind, as its settings",
          "[graph][core][midi-filter]") {
    FilterRig rig;
    SetGraphResult r = rig.set(doc(dropList({"noteOn", "sysex", "noteOn"})));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(r.ok);
    CHECK(GraphRig::codes(r) == "settings-invalid");
    CHECK(r.errors[0].nodeId == "f");
    CHECK(r.errors[0].message.find("drop names noteOn twice") != std::string::npos);
    r = rig.set(doc(dropList({"aftertouch"})));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(r.ok);
    CHECK(GraphRig::codes(r) == "settings-invalid");
    CHECK(rig.set(doc(R"({"drop":["noteOff","noteOn","polyAftertouch","controlChange","programChange",)"
                      R"("channelAftertouch","pitchBend","sysex","systemCommon","realtime"]})"))
              .ok);  // every kind, each once: the list's bound
}

TEST_CASE("rp.core.midi-filter's descriptor is its golden", "[graph][core][midi-filter]") {
    const rp_package* pkg = corePackage();
    const rp_node_type* type = nullptr;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < pkg->node_type_count; ++i)
        if (std::string_view(pkg->node_types[i]->id) == "rp.core.midi-filter") type = pkg->node_types[i];
    REQUIRE(type);
    const std::string json = type->descriptor(type);
    const std::string path = std::string(RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_DIR) + "/rp.core.midi-filter.descriptor.json";
    if (std::getenv("RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE")) std::ofstream(path) << json << "\n";
    CHECK(json == readFile(path));
    const auto parsed = parseDescriptor(json);
    REQUIRE(parsed);  // the strict parser takes it unchanged
    REQUIRE(parsed->layout.ports.size() == 2);
    CHECK(parsed->layout.ports[1].capacity.match == "in");
    CHECK_FALSE(parsed->heap);
    CHECK_FALSE(parsed->threads);
}
````

````diff
+TEST_CASE("a message's size is held to the room its queue has left, so no size wraps past the check",
+          "[graph][capacity]") {
+    std::vector<rp_message>   items(4);
+    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes(64);
+    rp_queue q{items.data(), 0, 4, bytes.data(), 0, 64, 0};
+    const std::uint8_t small[3] = {0x90, 60, 100};
+    REQUIRE(pushMessage(q, 0, small));
+    // A size that, added to the 3 bytes used, wraps std::size_t back to 1: the room left (61) is what it is held to,
+    // so it is dropped and counted rather than written. 0xFFFFFFFD is the same wrap (to 0) where size_t is 32 bits,
+    // as on the device, where a host supplies the length; here it is simply too large.
+    std::uint8_t* at = nullptr;
+    CHECK_FALSE(reserveMessage(q, 1, std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() - 1, 0, &at));
+    CHECK(at == nullptr);
+    CHECK_FALSE(reserveMessage(q, 1, std::size_t{0xFFFFFFFDu}, 0, &at));
+    CHECK(q.dropped == 2);
+    CHECK(q.count == 1);
+    CHECK(q.bytes_used == 3);
+    // Exactly the room left fits, one byte more does not.
+    CHECK_FALSE(reserveMessage(q, 2, 62, 0, &at));
+    CHECK(reserveMessage(q, 2, 61, 0, &at));
+    CHECK(q.bytes_used == 64);
+    CHECK(q.dropped == 3);
+}
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// A device host's MIDI input for the desktop's tests (rp.device.midi-in/1, graph/rp_device_midi_in.h): what a test
// stages before a block, handed out one message a call in staging order, and none again once it is all taken, as the
// box's host stages from its UART. Desktop-built: it allocates and frees as a test stages (a stage after a block that
// took everything starts the staging afresh), never in next.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "graph/rp_device_midi_in.h"

namespace rp::graph::devtest {

struct FakeMidiIn {
    struct Staged {
        std::uint32_t             frame;
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
        std::uint32_t             claimed = 0;  // a size to answer in place of the bytes' own (a host's bug), or 0
    };
    std::vector<Staged> staged;
    std::size_t         taken = 0;
    std::uint32_t       calls = 0;       // every call to next
    std::uint32_t       lastFrames = 0;  // the block length the last call named
    rp_device_midi_in   iface{this, &next};

    void stage(std::uint32_t frame, std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes) {
        if (taken == staged.size()) {
            staged.clear();
            taken = 0;
        }
        staged.push_back({frame, std::move(bytes), 0});
    }
    // A message whose answered size is `size`, whatever its bytes hold: what a broken host hands the node.
    void stageClaiming(std::uint32_t frame, std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes, std::uint32_t size) {
        stage(frame, std::move(bytes));
        staged.back().claimed = size;
    }

    static bool next(void* ctx, std::uint32_t frames, rp_device_midi_message* out) {
        auto* self = static_cast<FakeMidiIn*>(ctx);
        ++self->calls;
        self->lastFrames = frames;
        if (self->taken == self->staged.size()) return false;
        const Staged& s = self->staged[self->taken++];
        const auto size = s.claimed ? s.claimed : static_cast<std::uint32_t>(s.bytes.size());
        *out = rp_device_midi_message{s.frame, size, s.bytes.data()};
        return true;
    }
};

}  // namespace rp::graph::devtest
````

Create `packages/native/test/device-mode/FakeCart.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// A cart link that records what it is handed (CartRecord, DeviceModeEntries.hpp), built twice into
// retroplug-device-mode-test as PlanNodes.hpp's nodes are: in device mode by DeviceModeNodes.cpp, where it derives the
// device-mode build's rp::n8::CartLink (rp_devmode's), which is the one that build's rp.n8.nes casts its acquire to,
// and on the desktop by DevicePlan.test.cpp. Portable: no allocation, no lock.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "DeviceModeEntries.hpp"
#include "n8/CartLink.hpp"

namespace rp::graph::devtest {

class FakeCart final : public rp::n8::CartLink {
public:
    CartRecord* record = nullptr;

    bool push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush, double) override {
        if (!record) return false;
        if (!record->connected) {
            ++record->refused;
            return false;
        }
        if (record->count < CartRecord::kPushes) {
            CartPush& p = record->pushes[record->count];
            p.frame = frame;
            p.size = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size);
            p.flush = flush;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < size && i < sizeof p.bytes; ++i) p.bytes[i] = data[i];
        }
        ++record->count;
        return true;
    }
    bool          connected() const override { return record && record->connected; }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return record ? record->refused : 0; }
    void          setExpansionVolume(int value) override {
        if (record) record->volume = value;
    }
};

}  // namespace rp::graph::devtest
````

Create `packages/native/test/device-mode/DeviceIo.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// rp.device.midi-in (packages/device-io, docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 5), its device build and its
// desktop build alike, each made and run through the C ABI as a host makes it, over a fake rp.device.midi-in/1
// (FakeMidiIn.hpp).
//
// - It takes what the host staged for the block, in the host's order, at the host's frames: a frame at or past the
//   block's end lands on its last frame, one earlier than the last taken is clamped up to it, an empty message is not
//   pushed, and a block with nothing staged is empty. The host is told the block's length.
// - A full queue (256 messages, 4 KB) drops the rest and counts them as the queue's, and a message longer than the
//   queue's 4 KB is dropped and counted before its length reaches a push, whatever length the host answers.
// - A host that offers no rp.device.midi-in/1: it activates, every block is empty, and nothing faults.
// - The device build's create, activate, process and destroy allocate nothing; one a plan (`unique`).
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <sstream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "DeviceModeEntries.hpp"
#include "FakeMidiIn.hpp"
#include "graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "graph/GraphHost.hpp"
#include "graph/NodeRegistry.hpp"
#include "graph/Queue.hpp"
#include "graph/ResourceTable.hpp"
#include "graph/rp_device_midi_in.h"

namespace {

using rp::graph::devtest::FakeMidiIn;

void ignoreLog(void*, int, const char*) {}

// A host offering the fake's interface, or (with none) nothing at all.
struct MidiHost {
    FakeMidiIn* midi = nullptr;
    rp_host     host{RP_ABI_VERSION, this, nullptr, nullptr, &ignoreLog, &interface};
    static const void* interface(const rp_host* h, const char* id) {
        const auto* self = static_cast<const MidiHost*>(h->ctx);
        return self->midi && std::strcmp(id, RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_INTERFACE) == 0 ? &self->midi->iface : nullptr;
    }
};

const rp_node_type* midiInOf(const rp_package* p) {
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < p->node_type_count; ++i)
        if (std::string_view(p->node_types[i]->id) == "rp.device.midi-in") return p->node_types[i];
    return nullptr;
}

// One instance, made from msgpack's empty map (the node has no settings), activated, and run a block at a time into a
// queue of the node's own capacity, as a plan would give it.
struct Made {
    const rp_node_type*           type;
    std::vector<std::max_align_t> memory;
    rp_node*                      node = nullptr;
    bool                          active = false;
    std::vector<rp_message>       items = std::vector<rp_message>(RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES);
    std::vector<std::uint8_t>     bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>(RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES);
    rp_queue queue{items.data(), 0, RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES, bytes.data(), 0, RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES, 0};
    rp_transport transport{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, 0};

    Made(const rp_node_type* t, const rp_host* host) : type(t) {
        static const std::uint8_t kEmptyMap[] = {0x80};
        const rp_settings s{reinterpret_cast<const char*>(kEmptyMap), sizeof kEmptyMap, RP_SETTINGS_MSGPACK};
        rp_memory_req req{};
        rp_error      err{};
        REQUIRE(t->query_memory(t, &s, &req, &err));
        REQUIRE(req.align <= alignof(std::max_align_t));
        memory.resize(req.size / sizeof(std::max_align_t) + 1);
        node = t->create(t, host, memory.data(), &s, &err);
        INFO(err.message);
        REQUIRE(node);
        active = node->vt->activate(node, 48000.0, 1024, &err);
    }
    ~Made() {
        if (active) node->vt->deactivate(node);
        if (node) type->destroy(node);
    }
    Made(const Made&) = delete;
    Made& operator=(const Made&) = delete;

    rp_status block(std::uint32_t frames) {
        rp::graph::clearQueue(queue);
        queue.dropped = 0;
        rp_port_view out{};
        out.kind = RP_PORT_EVENTS;
        out.u.queue = &queue;
        const rp_process p{frames, &transport, nullptr, 0, &out, 1, nullptr, 0};
        return node->vt->process(node, &p);
    }
    // One line a message: frame and bytes.
    std::string taken() const {
        std::ostringstream o;
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < queue.count; ++i) {
            const rp_message& m = queue.items[i];
            o << m.frame << ":";
            for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < m.size; ++k) o << " " << std::hex << int(queue.bytes[m.offset + k]) << std::dec;
            o << "\n";
        }
        return o.str();
    }
};

// Both builds of the type: the device's, then the desktop's.
std::vector<const rp_node_type*> builds() {
    return {midiInOf(rp_device_io_package_device_mode()), midiInOf(rp_device_io_package())};
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("rp.device.midi-in takes what its host staged, at frames within the block, built for the device as for the "
          "desktop",
          "[device-mode][device-io]") {
    for (const rp_node_type* type : builds()) {
        REQUIRE(type);
        INFO((type == builds()[0] ? "device" : "desktop"));
        FakeMidiIn midi;
        MidiHost   host{&midi};
        Made       made(type, &host.host);
        REQUIRE(made.active);
        midi.stage(0, {0x90, 0x3c, 0x64});
        midi.stage(5, {0x80, 0x3c, 0x00});
        midi.stage(5, {0xB0, 0x07, 0x7f});
        midi.stage(63, {0xF8});
        midi.stage(64, {0xFA});              // at the block's end: its last frame
        midi.stage(70, {0xFC});              // past it: the same
        midi.stage(10, {0x90, 0x3e, 0x64});  // earlier than the last taken: clamped up to it
        midi.stage(12, {});                  // carries nothing: not pushed
        midi.stage(63, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x50, 0x01, 0xF7});
        CHECK(made.block(64) == RP_OK);
        CHECK(made.taken() == "0: 90 3c 64\n5: 80 3c 0\n5: b0 7 7f\n63: f8\n63: fa\n63: fc\n63: 90 3e 64\n"
                              "63: f0 7d 50 1 f7\n");
        CHECK(made.queue.dropped == 0);
        CHECK(midi.lastFrames == 64);
        CHECK(midi.calls == 10);  // nine messages, and the answer that none is left
        // Nothing staged: an empty block.
        CHECK(made.block(32) == RP_OK);
        CHECK(made.queue.count == 0);
        CHECK(midi.lastFrames == 32);
        CHECK(midi.calls == 11);
        // A one-frame block: everything at frame 0.
        midi.stage(0, {0xF8});
        midi.stage(9, {0xF8});
        CHECK(made.block(1) == RP_OK);
        CHECK(made.taken() == "0: f8\n0: f8\n");
    }
}

TEST_CASE("rp.device.midi-in drops what passes its 256 messages or 4 KB, and counts it", "[device-mode][device-io]") {
    for (const rp_node_type* type : builds()) {
        INFO((type == builds()[0] ? "device" : "desktop"));
        FakeMidiIn midi;
        MidiHost   host{&midi};
        Made       made(type, &host.host);
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < 300; ++i) midi.stage(i * 256 / 300, {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i & 0x7f), 1});
        CHECK(made.block(256) == RP_OK);
        CHECK(made.queue.count == RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES);
        CHECK(made.queue.dropped == 300 - RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES);
        CHECK(made.queue.items[255].frame == 255 * 256 / 300);  // the first 256, as staged
        // Two SysEx messages of 3000 bytes: the first fits the 4 KB, the second does not.
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> sysex(3000, 0x11);
        sysex.front() = 0xF0;
        sysex.back() = 0xF7;
        midi.stage(0, sysex);
        midi.stage(1, sysex);
        midi.stage(2, {0xF8});  // and a clock after it still fits
        CHECK(made.block(256) == RP_OK);
        CHECK(made.queue.count == 2);
        CHECK(made.queue.items[0].size == 3000);
        CHECK(made.queue.items[1].size == 1);
        CHECK(made.queue.dropped == 1);
        // A length past the queue's bytes, among small messages: 4097, and 0xFFFFFFFF after the one byte of F8 (a sum
        // that wraps to 0 in a 32-bit size_t), each dropped and counted; nothing is read from the bytes behind them.
        midi.stage(0, {0xF8});
        midi.stageClaiming(1, {0xF0, 0xF7}, RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES + 1);
        midi.stageClaiming(2, {0xF0, 0xF7}, 0xFFFFFFFFu);
        midi.stage(3, {0xFA});
        CHECK(made.block(256) == RP_OK);
        CHECK(made.taken() == "0: f8\n3: fa\n");
        CHECK(made.queue.dropped == 2);
        CHECK(made.queue.bytes_used == 2);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("rp.device.midi-in in a host that offers no rp.device.midi-in/1 activates, and gives empty blocks",
          "[device-mode][device-io]") {
    for (const rp_node_type* type : builds()) {
        INFO((type == builds()[0] ? "device" : "desktop"));
        MidiHost host;  // offers nothing
        Made     made(type, &host.host);
        CHECK(made.active);
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
            CHECK(made.block(64) == RP_OK);
            CHECK(made.queue.count == 0);
            CHECK(made.queue.dropped == 0);
        }
    }
}

TEST_CASE("rp.device.midi-in's device build allocates nothing, and a plan holds one", "[device-mode][device-io]") {
    FakeMidiIn midi;
    MidiHost   host{&midi};
    midi.staged.reserve(16);
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < 12; ++i) midi.stage(i * 5, {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i), 100});
    const rp_node_type* type = builds()[0];
    // The instance's memory and its queue are the host's, made before the window opens; its query_memory, create,
    // activate, block, deactivate and destroy are inside it. The window holds no Catch2 macro (which allocates).
    std::vector<std::max_align_t> memory(64);
    std::vector<rp_message>       items(RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES);
    std::vector<std::uint8_t>     bytes(RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES);
    static const std::uint8_t     kEmptyMap[] = {0x80};
    std::uint32_t                 count = 0;
    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations(rp::test::countsCAllocations());
    {
        const rp_settings s{reinterpret_cast<const char*>(kEmptyMap), sizeof kEmptyMap, RP_SETTINGS_MSGPACK};
        rp_memory_req     req{};
        rp_error          err{};
        const bool        sized = type->query_memory(type, &s, &req, &err) && req.size <= memory.size() * sizeof memory[0];
        rp_node*          node = sized ? type->create(type, &host.host, memory.data(), &s, &err) : nullptr;
        if (node && node->vt->activate(node, 48000.0, 1024, &err)) {
            rp_queue     q{items.data(), 0, RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES, bytes.data(), 0, RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES, 0};
            rp_port_view out{};
            out.kind = RP_PORT_EVENTS;
            out.u.queue = &q;
            const rp_transport t{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, 0};
            const rp_process   p{64, &t, nullptr, 0, &out, 1, nullptr, 0};
            node->vt->process(node, &p);
            count = q.count;
            node->vt->deactivate(node);
        }
        if (node) type->destroy(node);
    }
    const auto counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
    CHECK(count == 12);
    CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
    CHECK(counted.frees == 0);

    // `unique`, as the desktop's descriptor says and its planner holds.
    rp::graph::NodeRegistry registry;
    REQUIRE(registry.addPackage(rp_device_io_package()));
    rp::graph::ResourceTable resources;
    rp::graph::GraphHost     graph(registry, resources, rp::graph::HostConfig{48000.0, 256, rp::graph::Target::Pico});
    CHECK(graph.setGraph(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"a","type":"rp.device.midi-in"}],"wires":[]})").ok);
    const auto two = graph.setGraph(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"a","type":"rp.device.midi-in"},)"
                                    R"({"id":"b","type":"rp.device.midi-in"}],"wires":[]})");
    REQUIRE_FALSE(two.ok);
    CHECK(two.errors[0].code == "unique");
    CHECK(two.errors[0].nodeId == "b");
}
````

````diff
+// ---- the box's bridge ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+using devtest::FakeMidiIn;
+
+// The box's plan (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 5): the host's MIDI, BlipToaster's filter, the cart.
+const char* kBridge = R"({"nodes":[
+    {"id":"in","type":"rp.device.midi-in"},
+    {"id":"f","type":"rp.core.midi-filter","settings":{"drop":["polyAftertouch","channelAftertouch"]}},
+    {"id":"nes","type":"rp.n8.nes"}],
+  "wires":[{"from":"in.midi","to":"f.in"},{"from":"f.out","to":"nes.midi"}]})";
+
+// A block's staged MIDI, and whether the filter keeps each message.
+struct BridgeMessage {
+    std::uint32_t             frame;
+    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
+    bool                      kept;
+};
+const std::vector<std::vector<BridgeMessage>>& bridgeBlocks() {
+    static const std::vector<std::vector<BridgeMessage>> blocks = {
+        {{0, {0x90, 0x3c, 0x64}, true},
+         {3, {0xA0, 0x3c, 0x10}, false},
+         {4, {0xD0, 0x20}, false},
+         {4, {0xB0, 0x07, 0x64}, true},
+         {9, {0xF8}, true},
+         {10, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x50, 0x01, 0xF7}, true},
+         {20, {0xE0, 0x00, 0x40}, true}},
+        {},
+        {{1, {0x80, 0x3c, 0x00}, true}, {2, {0xA1, 0x40, 0x01}, false}, {30, {0xFA}, true}, {30, {0xD3, 0x7f}, false}},
+    };
+    return blocks;
+}
+
+// What a link should have been handed: each kept message at its frame, one line each.
+std::string keptLines() {
+    std::ostringstream o;
+    for (const auto& block : bridgeBlocks())
+        for (const BridgeMessage& m : block) {
+            if (!m.kept) continue;
+            o << m.frame << ":";
+            for (const std::uint8_t b : m.bytes) o << " " << std::hex << int(b) << std::dec;
+            o << "\n";
+        }
+    return o.str();
+}
+std::string pushedLines(const CartRecord& r) {
+    std::ostringstream o;
+    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < r.count && i < CartRecord::kPushes; ++i) {
+        o << r.pushes[i].frame << ":";
+        for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < r.pushes[i].size; ++k) o << " " << std::hex << int(r.pushes[i].bytes[k]) << std::dec;
+        o << "\n";
+    }
+    return o.str();
+}
+
+// A device host for the bridge: its cart link is `cart` (installed as the N8's, "n8" with rp.n8.cart-link/1) and its
+// MIDI input is `midi`.
+struct BridgeHost {
+    void*           cart = nullptr;
+    FakeMidiIn*     midi = nullptr;
+    rp_host_devices devices{this, &acquire, &release};
+    rp_host         host{RP_ABI_VERSION, this, nullptr, nullptr, &ignoreLog, &interface};
+    int             held = 0;
+
+    static void* acquire(void* ctx, const char* name, const char* id) {
+        auto* self = static_cast<BridgeHost*>(ctx);
+        if (std::strcmp(name, rp::n8::kDeviceName) != 0 || std::strcmp(id, rp::n8::kCartLinkInterface) != 0)
+            return nullptr;
+        ++self->held;
+        return self->cart;
+    }
+    static void release(void* ctx, void*) { --static_cast<BridgeHost*>(ctx)->held; }
+    static const void* lookup(const BridgeHost* self, const char* id) {
+        if (std::strcmp(id, RP_HOST_DEVICES_INTERFACE) == 0) return &self->devices;
+        if (std::strcmp(id, RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_INTERFACE) == 0) return &self->midi->iface;
+        return nullptr;
+    }
+    static const void* interface(const rp_host* h, const char* id) {
+        return lookup(static_cast<const BridgeHost*>(h->ctx), id);
+    }
+    // As GraphHost asks its embedder (HostConfig::interfaces).
+    static const void* embedded(void* ctx, const char* id) { return lookup(static_cast<const BridgeHost*>(ctx), id); }
+};
+
+void stageBlock(FakeMidiIn& midi, std::size_t block) {
+    for (const BridgeMessage& m : bridgeBlocks()[block]) midi.stage(m.frame, m.bytes);
+}
+

+TEST_CASE("the box's bridge, exported and loaded, hands the cart link what the filter keeps, in order, and never what "
+          "it drops",
+          "[device-mode][plan][device-io]") {
+    const ExportResult r = exported(kBridge);
+    INFO(described(r));
+    REQUIRE(r.ok());
+    constexpr std::uint32_t kBlock = 64;
+
+    // The loaded plan, over the device's builds and the device-mode fake link.
+    CartRecord device{};
+    FakeMidiIn deviceMidi;
+    BridgeHost deviceHost;
+    deviceHost.cart = rp_devtest_cart_device_mode(&device);
+    deviceHost.midi = &deviceMidi;
+    Arena         arena(kArenaBytes);
+    PlanLoadError err{};
+    LoadedPlan*   plan = loadPlan(r.blob, arena.span(kArenaBytes), deviceTypes(), &deviceHost.host, &err);
+    INFO(text(err.code) << " " << text(err.node) << ": " << text(err.message));
+    REQUIRE(plan);
+    CHECK(plan->nodes.size() == 3);
+    CHECK(deviceHost.held == 1);
+    for (std::size_t b = 0; b < bridgeBlocks().size(); ++b) {
+        stageBlock(deviceMidi, b);
+        runBlock(plan->view, kBlock, kTransport);
+    }
+    CHECK(plan->faults.load() == 0);
+    CHECK(plan->drops.load() == 0);
+    unloadPlan(plan);
+    CHECK(deviceHost.held == 0);
+
+    // GraphHost's run of the same document, over the desktop's builds and the desktop's fake link.
+    CartRecord             desktop{};
+    rp::graph::devtest::FakeCart desktopCart;
+    desktopCart.record = &desktop;
+    FakeMidiIn desktopMidi;
+    BridgeHost desktopHost;
+    desktopHost.cart = static_cast<rp::n8::CartLink*>(&desktopCart);
+    desktopHost.midi = &desktopMidi;
+    auto          registry = desktopRegistry();
+    ResourceTable resources;
+    HostConfig    config{48000.0, kMaxFrames, Target::Pico};
+    config.interfaces = &BridgeHost::embedded;
+    config.interfacesCtx = &desktopHost;
+    {
+        GraphHost host(*registry, resources, config);
+        REQUIRE(host.setGraph(kBridge).ok);
+        for (std::size_t b = 0; b < bridgeBlocks().size(); ++b) {
+            stageBlock(desktopMidi, b);
+            host.processBlock(kBlock, kTransport);
+        }
+        CHECK(host.faultCount() == 0);
+        CHECK(host.droppedMessages() == 0);
+    }
+
+    for (const CartRecord* rec : {&device, &desktop}) {
+        INFO((rec == &device ? "loaded" : "GraphHost"));
+        CHECK(pushedLines(*rec) == keptLines());
+        CHECK(rec->refused == 0);
+        CHECK(rec->volume == rp::n8::expansionVolumeRegister(rp::n8::kExpansionVolumeDefault));  // unity: 128
+        CHECK(rec->volume == 128);
+    }
+    // The dropped kinds never reached a push, and what reached one is every message of the others.
+    std::size_t staged = 0, kept = 0;
+    for (const auto& block : bridgeBlocks())
+        for (const BridgeMessage& m : block) {
+            ++staged;
+            kept += m.kept;
+        }
+    CHECK(device.count == kept);
+    CHECK(kept < staged);
+}
````

````bash
feat(graph): rp.core.midi-filter and rp.device.midi-in, the box plan's first two nodes

rp.core.midi-filter (packages/core, portable) drops the MIDI messages of the kinds its `drop` names and passes every
other one as it came, frame, flags, bytes and order kept. A kind is the status byte's (the seven channel messages by
their high nibble, then sysex for F0 and a lone F7, systemCommon for F1 to F6, realtime for F8 to FF): an events
message is one MIDI message led by its status, and a message led by a data byte is of no kind and passes, since the
filter keeps no running status. `drop` is an rp::list of rp::choice bounded by the ten kinds, and validate refuses a
kind named twice. Every desktop product lists core, so the [packages] golden gains the type id in each, and the type
has its own descriptor golden.

The filter's output is sized as whatever feeds its input, so it never drops what its source could carry. No node could
say that before, so a queue capacity may now be `{"match": "<input>"}` in place of a size (rp::events_out::matching
<"in"> in the authoring layer, defineNode's events.out({ match }) in TS): the layout parse holds it to one of the node's
inputs of the output's own kind, and the planner resolves it from the wires (a feedback wire's source too; an unwired input
gives the default; a loop of matches is refused, code capacity-match). Layouts keep it as declared.

rp.device.midi-in (packages/device-io, a new workspace package, `device: true`) reads a device host's MIDI input,
rp.device.midi-in/1 (graph/rp_device_midi_in.h, in the SDK since the hosts that offer it, the box's library, a test's
fake and the exporter's stub, include nothing of a pack's). The host stages whole messages at frames of the next
block; the node takes them onto a `midi` output of 256 messages and 4 KB, clamping a frame past the block's end and one
out of order, counting a full queue's drops as its own, and a message longer than the queue's bytes before its length
reaches a push. reserveMessage (graph/Queue.hpp) holds a size to the room left rather than to a sum, which a host's
length near UINT32_MAX would wrap on a 32-bit device; every queue keeps bytes_used within its capacity, so each
decision on the desktop is the one the sum made, and no desktop byte moves. It is `unique`, and a host that offers no interface gives it
empty blocks, never a fault. Desktop products do not list the package; the exporter does (its stub host now offers an
input with nothing staged), and so does the device check, whose device-mode test holds every device entry to its list.

Tests: the filter through real plans in retroplug-graph-test (each kind alone, the box plan's two aftertouches, the
first-byte rule, the matched capacity against a default one, no allocation, the refusals, the golden), capacity
matching in the planner and the descriptor parser, and the TS twin; in retroplug-device-mode-test, the filter's device
build against its desktop build in the twin table (over a source of every kind), rp.device.midi-in's two builds over a
fake input, and the box's bridge (rp.device.midi-in into the filter into rp.n8.nes) exported, loaded and run over a
fake cart link, which receives what the filter keeps, in order, and the expansion volume at unity, as GraphHost's run
of the same document gives its own.
````

---

### Task 3: the box as a graph host, its bridge a built-in plan

Design sections 5 and 7 and section 9's third commit. The Pico box runs a graph. `pico/host/` is a library with no N8
in it: the device `rp_host` (`rp.host.devices/2` over a table a product fills, `rp.device.midi-in/1` over the staged
MIDI), the built-in plan's load into a static arena and its blocks, the block driver behind the seam `next(frames,
transport)`, and the UART MIDI path (the interrupt's ring with its timestamps, `midi.c`'s parser, the staging). The
host ends each block itself, dropping (counted) what the block did not take, so the parse and the box's own `F0 7D 50`
commands never stop. `pico/n8-host/` keeps the N8 flows as they were and gains `BoxCartLink` (a fixed ring the main
loop drains after the block in FIFO writes of up to 192 bytes, refusing and counting pushes while no game runs,
writing `rp.n8.nes`'s expansion volume at every connect and on a change), `BoxStats` and `CartVolume`; `plan.json`
(`rp.device.midi-in` -> `rp.core.midi-filter` -> `rp.n8.nes`, 48 kHz, 256 frames) is exported at build time by
`retroplug-export-plan` against the 128 KiB arena and embedded. The image reserves no heap, every frame of both device
images is held to 1 KiB (`-Werror=stack-usage=1024`), and the box runs from SRAM (`copy_to_ram`), which is what keeps
an isolated message's latency at E2's. `-DN8_LAT_TRACE=1` builds the latency trace, off by default.

The pieces the packages share come first (one note rule, a never-inlined fallback), then the stack limit, the host
library, the box's link, the firmware, the desktop tests of the box's portable pieces, and the scripts. Nothing is
flashed or run on the rig here: the gate is Task 6's, the controller's. A red comes first, on Task 2's binary as it
is; the tree is built once, in Step 9: build nothing in Steps 2 to 8.

- [ ] **Step 2: What the packages share: one note rule and a never-inlined fallback**

`graph/noinline.hpp` is `RP_NOINLINE` (GCC/Clang's `noinline`, MSVC's `__declspec(noinline)`), one macro for what were
three. `PlanLoader.cpp` moves the `PlanLoadError` fallback that `loadPlan` and `sizePlan` keep for a caller passing no
error into never-inlined helpers: `loadPlan` was the one frame past 1 KiB (1120 bytes, 352 of them that fallback), and
is 768 now; behaviour is unchanged. The N8 pack's `Ops.cpp` takes the shared macro for its `writeBattery`.
`n8/CartLink.hpp` gains `rp::n8::NoteEvent noteEvent(data, size)`, the note rule `rp.n8.nes`'s `pushMidi` and the
box's link both keep their books by, and `N8Node.cpp` uses it: the node's behaviour is unchanged.

Create `packages/node-sdk/native/src/graph/noinline.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// RP_NOINLINE: the never-inlined form of a function, so its frame is on the stack only while it runs. What a device
// build uses to keep a large local (an error kept for a caller that asked for none, a whole console line, a file path)
// off the frame of the function that calls it, which -Wstack-usage measures (cmake/device-image.cmake).
#if defined(_MSC_VER)
#define RP_NOINLINE __declspec(noinline)
#else
#define RP_NOINLINE __attribute__((noinline))
#endif
````

````diff
+struct NoteEvent {

+inline NoteEvent noteEvent(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {

+    n.off = kind == 0x80 || (kind == 0x90 && data[2] == 0);
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The stack limit, and the parser cleaned for the desktop's compilers**

`cmake/device-image.cmake` sets `RP_DEVICE_STACK_FRAME` (1024) and appends `-Werror=stack-usage=1024` to
`RP_DEVICE_COMPILE_OPTIONS`, which every package library a device project builds takes, and `rp_device_executable()`
adds it to each image, whose compile includes the SDK's, TinyUSB's and Pico-PIO-USB's sources; it holds in Release and
Debug. The file must now be included after `RP_DEVICE_COMPILE_OPTIONS` is set and before the first package, and
refuses otherwise, each in its own words ("include device-image.cmake before the first retroplug_package(), so the
packages' libraries are held to the stack limit" and "set RP_DEVICE_COMPILE_OPTIONS (the SDK's code-generation
options) before including device-image.cmake"); it says how a vendored frame past the limit is to be handled (that one
source's own limit, with a comment, never the flag taken off a target). `rp-device-check`'s `CMakeLists.txt` includes
it in that place; the flag alone changes no byte of its image (the stage's first build under it was Task 2's image
exactly). `pico/midi-in/midi.c` gains explicit `(uint8_t)` casts and writes its designated initializer as assignments,
so it compiles in the desktop test under `/W4 /WX`; its behaviour is unchanged.

````diff
+# the build naming the function. That is the measure of a node's stack in query_memory and create that E1 asked for, in
+# place of a hand sum: it bounds each frame, not a chain of them, and the chains are still the images' own word
+# (pico/n8-host/CMakeLists.txt's for the box). 1 KiB is a quarter of the 4 KB main stack the box gives. The limit is
+# on in every build type, and both the shipped Release (-O3) and the Debug Probe's Debug (-Og) builds of both images

+#
+# A frame past the limit is fixed where it is ours: a large local moved into a frame of its own (RP_NOINLINE,
+# graph/noinline.hpp) or off the stack. Where it is a vendored source's (a later SDK, TinyUSB or Pico-PIO-USB), the
+# remedy is that one source's own limit, a COMPILE_OPTIONS property on it (set_source_files_properties) raising
+# -Werror=stack-usage for it alone, beside a comment naming the function, its frame and why the chain still fits; never

+# rp_device_executable(<target> <sources>...): an executable as a device builds it: the device-mode flags, the stack
+# limit, the runtime and the trap. One --wrap a symbol: -Wl, splits at commas, so a joined list would hand the linker
+# the symbols as input files.
 function(rp_device_executable target)

+                           "-Werror=stack-usage=${_frame}")
     target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE pico_stdlib)
     get_property(_trapped GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_DEVICE_TRAPPED)
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The generic box host, `pico/host/`**

`host.cmake` lists the portable sources (everything but the UART's) for the desktop's tests and, in a device project,
makes `rp-box-host` an INTERFACE library, as the SDK's are, so its sources take the image's flags and stack limit.
`BlockDriver`: the seam and E3's `ElapsedDriver`, frames counted from the start on a 64-bit microsecond clock, each
block `min(due - done, maxFrames)`, the carry bounded at `kCarryBlocks` (4) blocks with the excess dropped and counted
(`skipped()`), and `frameOf(us32)` placing a 32-bit UART timestamp on the current block, clamped into it.
`MidiStaging`: `midi.c`'s parser fed byte by byte with timestamps; every message staged whole with its status byte
(running status restored, system common and real time included), a SysEx assembled whole in its own 4 KB buffer and
staged at its F7 or at the status that cut it short, one past 4096 bytes dropped whole (`tooLong`), the product's
SysEx hook offered each complete SysEx first; `feed()` refuses a byte, taking nothing, when the staging could not hold
what it might complete, so it waits in the UART ring; `next()` hands messages out in order; `endBlock()` drops,
counted (`untaken`), what a block did not take, then stages what waited for room; `arrival(frame, bytes)` answers when
a handed message arrived, for the link's latency. `DeviceHost`: the device `rp_host`, no allocation, no jobs, no
resources. `BuiltInPlan`: `load` (Task 1's loader) printing the plan, its nodes and their bytes, or the refusal's two
lines; `run(driver)`, never more than `maxFrames`; each faulted node printed once. `UartMidi` (Pico SDK): the UART1
interrupt, its 4096-byte timestamped ring (`static_assert`ed to `RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES`) and counters, moved from
`main.cpp`, the masked idle poll, the drain into the staging and the discard.

Create `pico/host/host.cmake`:

````cmake
# pico/host (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 5): the generic box host, a library with no N8 in it. The
# device rp_host and its two interfaces (DeviceHost), the built-in plan's load and its blocks (BuiltInPlan), the block
# driver (BlockDriver), and the UART MIDI path: the interrupt's ring with its timestamps (UartMidi), the parser
# (pico/midi-in's midi.c) and the staging (MidiStaging). A box product (pico/n8-host) includes this file and links
# rp-box-host; the desktop's tests (packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake) include it for the portable sources, which they
# build for the host.
include_guard(GLOBAL)

set(RP_BOX_HOST_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}")
# Everything but the UART's own code, which needs the Pico SDK: what the desktop's tests build as the box does.
set(RP_BOX_HOST_PORTABLE_SOURCES
    "${RP_BOX_HOST_DIR}/BlockDriver.cpp"
    "${RP_BOX_HOST_DIR}/BuiltInPlan.cpp"
    "${RP_BOX_HOST_DIR}/DeviceHost.cpp"
    "${RP_BOX_HOST_DIR}/MidiStaging.cpp"
    "${RP_BOX_HOST_DIR}/../midi-in/midi.c")
set(RP_BOX_HOST_INCLUDES "${RP_BOX_HOST_DIR}" "${RP_BOX_HOST_DIR}/../midi-in")

# In a device project (the Pico SDK's, after pico_sdk_init and the packages), an INTERFACE library, as the SDK's own
# are: its sources compile in the image that links it, with that image's device flags and stack limit.
if(PICO_SDK_VERSION_STRING)
    add_library(rp-box-host INTERFACE)
    target_sources(rp-box-host INTERFACE ${RP_BOX_HOST_PORTABLE_SOURCES} "${RP_BOX_HOST_DIR}/UartMidi.cpp")
    target_include_directories(rp-box-host INTERFACE ${RP_BOX_HOST_INCLUDES})
    target_link_libraries(rp-box-host INTERFACE pico_stdlib hardware_uart retroplug-graph-exec)
endif()
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The block driver (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 5): the seam between what sets a box's cadence and
// the plan it runs. One call, next(): whether a block is due, how many frames it covers and the transport it runs
// under. E3's driver (ElapsedDriver) answers the time since the previous block; an audio driver later answers its fixed
// block when its buffer is ready, and neither the loader nor a node changes with it.
//
// Portable (no Pico SDK), so the desktop's tests build it as the box does.

#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_node.h"

namespace rp::box {

class BlockDriver {
public:
    // The next block: true with its length in *frames (at least 1, at most the plan's maxFrames) and *transport
    // filled, or false when none is due.
    virtual bool next(std::uint32_t* frames, rp_transport* transport) = 0;

protected:
    ~BlockDriver() = default;
};

// E3's driver: the time since the previous block at the plan's sample rate, in whole frames, carrying what passes
// maxFrames into the next block. The frames are counted from the start rather than block by block, so the frames run
// add up to the time passed, its fraction of a frame included: no frame is lost or run twice while the carry is
// within kCarryBlocks blocks (21.3 ms at 48 kHz and 256 frames). That carries an 11 ms console line or a 5 ms FIFO
// write whole. A longer hold (an N8 call of 20 ms or more, a boot through the N8's menu, a 12 s install: 576,000
// frames), or passes that keep outlasting a block (one block runs a pass, so a stream whose passes each spend more
// than a block's time in FIFO writes falls behind until it reaches the bound), drops the frames past the bound,
// counted (skipped(), the box's [stats] `skipped=`), rather than running them: run, a long wait would be thousands of
// empty blocks, and under a stream the catch-up would last minutes with every message stamped at its block's last
// frame. Bounded, the driver is at most kCarryBlocks blocks behind the clock, a message lands within 21 ms of its
// frame, and the passes after a wait do no extra work. Nothing in the box's bridge plan reads time; a plan that does
// (a MIDI clock, say) would lose the dropped time under load, which is the audio driver's to settle: a fixed cadence
// has no carry.
//
// A message waits for no block of its own: when a pass comes less than a frame's time (20.8 us) after the last block,
// next() has no block, and what was staged goes to the next pass's block, a pass later.
class ElapsedDriver final : public BlockDriver {
public:
    // Microseconds, monotonic, from any origin.
    using Clock = std::uint64_t (*)(void* ctx);

    // The most blocks' worth of frames a next() finds due and runs (one now, the rest in the passes after); time past
    // it is dropped.
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kCarryBlocks = 4;

    // Starts the timeline at the clock's now: the first block covers the time from here. `maxFrames` is the plan's,
    // which a block never passes (runBlock does not check it).
    void start(Clock clock, void* ctx, std::uint32_t sampleRate, std::uint32_t maxFrames);
    bool next(std::uint32_t* frames, rp_transport* transport) override;

    // The frame a moment (the low 32 bits of the clock's microseconds, as a UART timestamp holds them) falls on within
    // the block the last next() answered: its offset from the block's first frame, clamped into the block. A moment
    // before the block (a message that waited a pass, or one in time the bound dropped) is its first frame and one
    // after it (the block runs behind the clock, with a carry) its last, so a message is never held for a later block.
    std::uint32_t frameOf(std::uint32_t us) const;

    // The frames due and not yet run, as of the last next().
    std::uint64_t carried() const { return due_ - done_; }
    // Blocks run since the start.
    std::uint64_t blocks() const { return blocks_; }
    // Frames dropped for falling past the carry's bound.
    std::uint64_t skipped() const { return skipped_; }

private:
    std::uint64_t frameAt(std::uint64_t us) const;

    Clock         clock_ = nullptr;
    void*         ctx_ = nullptr;
    std::uint32_t rate_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t maxFrames_ = 0;
    std::uint64_t origin_ = 0;   // the clock at the start
    std::uint64_t now_ = 0;      // the clock at the last next()
    std::uint64_t due_ = 0;      // frames from the start to now_
    std::uint64_t done_ = 0;     // frames run
    std::uint64_t first_ = 0;    // the first frame of the last block answered
    std::uint32_t frames_ = 0;   // its length
    std::uint64_t blocks_ = 0;
    std::uint64_t skipped_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace rp::box
````

Create `pico/host/BlockDriver.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "BlockDriver.hpp"

namespace rp::box {

void ElapsedDriver::start(Clock clock, void* ctx, std::uint32_t sampleRate, std::uint32_t maxFrames) {
    clock_ = clock;
    ctx_ = ctx;
    rate_ = sampleRate;
    maxFrames_ = maxFrames;
    origin_ = now_ = clock_(ctx_);
    due_ = done_ = first_ = blocks_ = skipped_ = 0;
    frames_ = 0;
}

// Whole frames from the start to `us`: 64-bit, so a box up for years at 48 kHz neither wraps nor rounds.
std::uint64_t ElapsedDriver::frameAt(std::uint64_t us) const {
    return us <= origin_ ? 0 : (us - origin_) * rate_ / 1000000u;
}

bool ElapsedDriver::next(std::uint32_t* frames, rp_transport* transport) {
    if (!clock_ || rate_ == 0 || maxFrames_ == 0) return false;
    now_ = clock_(ctx_);
    due_ = frameAt(now_);
    if (due_ <= done_) return false;
    const std::uint64_t bound = std::uint64_t{kCarryBlocks} * maxFrames_;
    if (due_ - done_ > bound) {
        skipped_ += due_ - done_ - bound;
        done_ = due_ - bound;
    }
    const std::uint64_t owed = due_ - done_;
    frames_ = owed > maxFrames_ ? maxFrames_ : static_cast<std::uint32_t>(owed);
    first_ = done_;
    done_ += frames_;
    ++blocks_;
    *frames = frames_;
    // The box keeps no musical time: nothing plays, at the tempo every host gives a stopped transport.
    *transport = rp_transport{static_cast<double>(rate_), 120.0, 0.0, 0u};
    return true;
}

std::uint32_t ElapsedDriver::frameOf(std::uint32_t us) const {
    if (frames_ == 0) return 0;
    // The moment on the 64-bit clock: `us` is at most one wrap of the 32-bit microseconds (71 minutes) before now_,
    // which a timestamp of a message staged since the last block always is.
    const std::uint32_t ago = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(now_) - us;
    const std::uint64_t at = now_ >= ago ? now_ - ago : 0;
    const std::uint64_t frame = frameAt(at);
    if (frame <= first_) return 0;
    const std::uint64_t offset = frame - first_;
    return offset >= frames_ ? frames_ - 1 : static_cast<std::uint32_t>(offset);
}

}  // namespace rp::box
````

Create `pico/host/MidiStaging.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// A box's MIDI input (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 5): the bytes off its MIDI UART, each with the
// moment it arrived, parsed into whole messages by pico/midi-in's parser (midi.c) and staged for rp.device.midi-in,
// which takes them through the host's rp.device.midi-in/1 (graph/rp_device_midi_in.h) at the frame of the block each
// arrival falls on. The host filters nothing: every message is staged as it came, with its status byte (a message the
// sender sent under running status gets its status back), system common and real time among them, save a complete
// SysEx the product's hook takes (the box's own F0 7D 50 commands). What one cart wants dropped is its plan's business.
//
// A SysEx is staged whole, once its F7 (or the status byte that cut it short, for which the parser supplies the F7)
// has arrived, so it is one message of one kind and a filter that drops `sysex` drops all of it. One past the 4 KB a
// message may be (RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES) is dropped whole and counted.
//
// What a block takes is bounded (RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES and _BYTES, rp.device.midi-in's queue), and feed() is
// bounded the same way: it refuses a byte when the staging could not take the message that byte might complete, taking
// nothing, and the caller leaves the byte in its ring for the next pass, after the block has emptied the staging. So
// the staging loses nothing to its own size, and a burst past one block's worth waits a pass rather than being dropped.
//
// The host ends each block itself (endBlock(), after runBlock): what the block did not take is dropped and counted,
// whatever the plan is. A plan with no rp.device.midi-in, or one whose midi-in the executor has silenced for a fault,
// takes nothing, and the staging must still empty, or feed() would refuse every byte from then on and the parse (the
// box's own commands among it) would stop. A host with no plan at all drops what is staged each pass
// (clearStaged()).
//
// Portable (no Pico SDK), so the desktop's tests build it as the box does. One thread: the main loop feeds it and runs
// the block whose rp.device.midi-in drains it.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_device_midi_in.h"
#include "midi.h"

namespace rp::box {

class MidiStaging {
public:
    // What one block takes: rp.device.midi-in's queue, which the host stages no more than.
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kMessages = RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES;
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kBytes = RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES;
    static_assert(kMessages == 256 && kBytes == 4096, "the box stages what rp.device.midi-in takes in a block");
    // The longest message, a SysEx with its F0 and F7: the most one message may carry in rp.device.midi-in's queue.
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kSysexBytes = RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES;

    // A complete SysEx, F0 to F7, before it is staged: true takes it (it is not staged). The box's own commands.
    using SysexHook = bool (*)(void* ctx, const std::uint8_t* data, std::uint32_t size);
    // The frame a moment falls on within the block being run (ElapsedDriver::frameOf): what next() stamps each message
    // with, read when the block takes it.
    using FrameOf = std::uint32_t (*)(void* ctx, std::uint32_t us);

    struct Counts {
        std::uint32_t channelMessages = 0;  // complete channel-voice messages parsed (the box's `msgs`)
        std::uint32_t handed = 0;           // messages handed to the plan (rp.device.midi-in took them)
        std::uint32_t consumed = 0;         // SysEx messages the hook took
        std::uint32_t tooLong = 0;          // SysEx messages past kSysexBytes, dropped whole
        std::uint32_t untaken = 0;          // staged messages no block took (endBlock, clearStaged), dropped
    };

    // Zero until init(), which runs before the first byte: a box's one staging is in static storage, in .bss, with
    // nothing copied out of flash for it.
    constexpr MidiStaging() = default;
    void init(SysexHook hook, void* hookCtx, FrameOf frameOf, void* frameCtx);

    // One byte off the UART and when it arrived (the low 32 bits of the microsecond clock): false, taking nothing,
    // when the staging could not hold what it might complete.
    bool feed(std::uint8_t byte, std::uint32_t arrivedUs);
    // Drops what is staged and the parse in progress, as a stream starting over: the box's stale MIDI, discarded when
    // forwarding begins.
    void reset();
    // Drops what is staged and keeps the parse, counted: for a host with no plan to take it, so its parse (the box's
    // commands) goes on.
    void clearStaged();
    // After a block: drops what it did not take, counted, and stages what waited for its room (a SysEx held whole, and
    // the short message behind it) for the next block, with no byte to wait for.
    void endBlock();

    // The interface rp.device.midi-in reads, whose next() hands the staged messages out in order, each at its frame.
    const rp_device_midi_in* interface() const { return &interface_; }
    // [audio] When the message the block handed out at `frame` with these bytes arrived, for a link timing what it was
    // given: the first one this block handed out at that frame with the same bytes, not yet asked for, the messages
    // asked for in order (a node keeps its input's order). A message the plan dropped is passed over, since none with
    // its bytes is asked for in its place (a filter keeps or drops by kind, so equal bytes share a fate). False for a
    // message none was handed out as, which a node's own message (rp.n8.nes's note-offs) is, with one exception: a
    // node's own message asked for first, at a frame and with the bytes of one the block handed out (an owed note-off
    // paid at frame 0 when the input carries the same note-off at frame 0), takes that one's arrival, and the input's
    // own push, and any earlier one at that frame with other bytes, find none and are timed from now. Only the latency
    // figure moves, in the block after a reconnect.
    bool arrival(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t* us);

    const Counts& counts() const { return counts_; }
    std::uint32_t staged() const { return count_ - read_; }

private:
    struct Entry {
        std::uint32_t at;      // arrival, microseconds
        std::uint32_t frame;   // the frame next() handed it out at
        std::uint16_t offset;  // into bytes_
        std::uint16_t size;
    };

    static void onMessage(const midi_message* m, void* user);
    static void onSysex(std::uint8_t b, void* user);
    static bool nextFn(void* ctx, std::uint32_t frames, rp_device_midi_message* out);

    bool fits(std::uint32_t size) const { return count_ < kMessages && size <= kBytes - used_; }
    void stage(const std::uint8_t* data, std::uint32_t size, std::uint32_t at);
    void place(const std::uint8_t* data, std::uint32_t size, std::uint32_t at);
    void sysexDone();
    bool flushPending();

    SysexHook hook_ = nullptr;
    void*     hookCtx_ = nullptr;
    FrameOf   frameOf_ = nullptr;
    void*     frameCtx_ = nullptr;
    rp_device_midi_in interface_{};  // init() points it here

    midi_parser   parser_{};
    std::uint32_t now_ = 0;  // the arrival of the byte being parsed

    // The staging: the messages of the next block, their bytes back to back.
    Entry         entries_[kMessages] = {};
    std::uint8_t  bytes_[kBytes] = {};
    std::uint32_t count_ = 0, used_ = 0, read_ = 0;

    // The SysEx being parsed, and once complete, held while the staging has no room for it (`sysexHeld_`), with at
    // most one short message the same byte completed behind it (`short_`), so the order is kept.
    std::uint8_t  sysex_[kSysexBytes] = {};
    std::uint32_t sysexSize_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t sysexAt_ = 0;
    bool          sysexOpen_ = false, sysexOver_ = false, sysexHeld_ = false;
    std::uint8_t  short_[3] = {};
    std::uint32_t shortSize_ = 0, shortAt_ = 0;

    std::uint32_t asked_ = 0;  // arrival()'s place among what this block handed out

    Counts counts_{};
};

}  // namespace rp::box
````

Create `pico/host/MidiStaging.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "MidiStaging.hpp"

#include <cstring>

namespace rp::box {

void MidiStaging::init(SysexHook hook, void* hookCtx, FrameOf frameOf, void* frameCtx) {
    hook_ = hook;
    hookCtx_ = hookCtx;
    frameOf_ = frameOf;
    frameCtx_ = frameCtx;
    interface_ = rp_device_midi_in{this, &nextFn};
    reset();
}

void MidiStaging::reset() {
    midi_parser_init(&parser_, &onMessage, this);
    midi_parser_set_sysex_sink(&parser_, &onSysex);
    sysexOpen_ = sysexOver_ = false;
    sysexSize_ = 0;
    count_ = used_ = read_ = asked_ = 0;
    sysexHeld_ = false;
    shortSize_ = 0;
}

void MidiStaging::clearStaged() {
    counts_.untaken += count_ - read_ + (sysexHeld_ ? 1u : 0u) + (shortSize_ != 0 ? 1u : 0u);
    count_ = used_ = read_ = asked_ = 0;
    sysexHeld_ = false;
    shortSize_ = 0;
}

void MidiStaging::endBlock() {
    counts_.untaken += count_ - read_;
    count_ = used_ = read_ = asked_ = 0;
    flushPending();
}

bool MidiStaging::feed(std::uint8_t byte, std::uint32_t arrivedUs) {
    if (!flushPending()) return false;
    // Whatever this byte completes: a message of up to three bytes, or (a status byte inside a SysEx) the SysEx and at
    // most one such message after it, the two held while the staging has no room (sysexDone, stage).
    if (!fits(3)) return false;
    now_ = arrivedUs;
    midi_parser_byte(&parser_, byte);
    return true;
}

// A message the parser completed, rebuilt with its status byte: a channel message is 3 bytes but for a program change
// and channel pressure (2), real time 1, and system common as long as its status says (the song position 3, the time
// code and song select 2, the rest 1).
void MidiStaging::onMessage(const midi_message* m, void* user) {
    auto&              self = *static_cast<MidiStaging*>(user);
    const std::uint8_t data[3] = {m->status, m->data0, m->data1};
    std::uint32_t      size = 1;
    if (m->status < 0xF0) {
        ++self.counts_.channelMessages;
        size = m->type == MIDI_PROGRAM_CHANGE || m->type == MIDI_CHANNEL_PRESSURE ? 2 : 3;
    } else if (m->status == 0xF2) {
        size = 3;
    } else if (m->status == 0xF1 || m->status == 0xF3) {
        size = 2;
    }
    self.stage(data, size, self.now_);
}

void MidiStaging::onSysex(std::uint8_t b, void* user) {
    auto& self = *static_cast<MidiStaging*>(user);
    if (b == 0xF0) {
        self.sysexOpen_ = true;
        self.sysexOver_ = false;
        self.sysexSize_ = 0;
    }
    if (!self.sysexOpen_) return;
    if (self.sysexSize_ < kSysexBytes)
        self.sysex_[self.sysexSize_++] = b;
    else
        self.sysexOver_ = true;
    if (b == 0xF7) {
        self.sysexOpen_ = false;
        self.sysexDone();
    }
}

void MidiStaging::sysexDone() {
    if (sysexOver_) {
        ++counts_.tooLong;
        return;
    }
    if (hook_ && hook_(hookCtx_, sysex_, sysexSize_)) {
        ++counts_.consumed;
        return;
    }
    sysexAt_ = now_;
    if (fits(sysexSize_))
        place(sysex_, sysexSize_, sysexAt_);
    else
        sysexHeld_ = true;  // feed() takes nothing more until a block has made room for it
}

// A short message, staged, or held behind a held SysEx (or when a SysEx the same byte completed took the room): feed()
// checked for its room before the byte, and one byte completes at most one short message.
void MidiStaging::stage(const std::uint8_t* data, std::uint32_t size, std::uint32_t at) {
    if (!sysexHeld_ && fits(size)) {
        place(data, size, at);
        return;
    }
    std::memcpy(short_, data, size);
    shortSize_ = size;
    shortAt_ = at;
}

void MidiStaging::place(const std::uint8_t* data, std::uint32_t size, std::uint32_t at) {
    entries_[count_++] = Entry{at, 0, static_cast<std::uint16_t>(used_), static_cast<std::uint16_t>(size)};
    std::memcpy(bytes_ + used_, data, size);
    used_ += size;
}

bool MidiStaging::flushPending() {
    if (sysexHeld_) {
        if (!fits(sysexSize_)) return false;
        place(sysex_, sysexSize_, sysexAt_);
        sysexHeld_ = false;
    }
    if (shortSize_ != 0) {
        if (!fits(shortSize_)) return false;
        place(short_, shortSize_, shortAt_);
        shortSize_ = 0;
    }
    return true;
}

bool MidiStaging::nextFn(void* ctx, std::uint32_t frames, rp_device_midi_message* out) {
    auto& self = *static_cast<MidiStaging*>(ctx);
    if (self.read_ == self.count_) return false;  // the host empties the staging after the block (endBlock)
    Entry&        e = self.entries_[self.read_++];
    std::uint32_t frame = self.frameOf_ ? self.frameOf_(self.frameCtx_, e.at) : 0;
    if (frame >= frames) frame = frames != 0 ? frames - 1 : 0;
    e.frame = frame;
    *out = rp_device_midi_message{frame, e.size, self.bytes_ + e.offset};
    ++self.counts_.handed;
    return true;
}

bool MidiStaging::arrival(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t* us) {
    while (asked_ < read_ && entries_[asked_].frame < frame) ++asked_;
    for (std::uint32_t i = asked_; i < read_ && entries_[i].frame == frame; ++i) {
        const Entry& e = entries_[i];
        if (e.size != size || std::memcmp(bytes_ + e.offset, data, size) != 0) continue;
        *us = e.at;
        asked_ = i + 1;
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}

}  // namespace rp::box
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// A box's rp_host (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 5): what the nodes of its plan are created under. It
// offers two interfaces and nothing else: rp.host.devices/2 over a small table of links the product fills (the N8 box's
// cart link, installed as "n8" with rp.n8.cart-link/1), and rp.device.midi-in/1, the staged MIDI (MidiStaging). No
// heap (alloc and free are null, as a target with none has them), no rp.host.jobs/1 (a node that would run a device job
// is told "this host takes no device jobs"), no resources.
//
// Portable (no Pico SDK), so the desktop's tests build it as the box does.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_device.h"
#include "graph/rp_device_midi_in.h"
#include "graph/rp_node.h"

namespace rp::box {

// One link a host installs: the name and the interface id a node acquires it by (RP_DEVICE_NAME_MAX and
// RP_DEVICE_INTERFACE_ID_MAX bound them), the link as that interface's pointer, and the link's own hooks, told of each
// acquire and release (a cart link counts the nodes holding it). Either hook may be null.
struct DeviceLink {
    const char* name;
    const char* interfaceId;
    void*       link;
    void*       hookCtx;
    void (*acquired)(void* ctx);
    void (*released)(void* ctx);
};

class DeviceHost {
public:
    // A line the host's nodes log, with its RP_LOG_* level.
    using Log = void (*)(int level, const char* message);

    constexpr DeviceHost() = default;
    // The links are the caller's and outlive every plan created under this host.
    void init(const DeviceLink* links, std::size_t count, const rp_device_midi_in* midi, Log log);

    const rp_host* host() const { return &host_; }

private:
    static void*       acquireFn(void* ctx, const char* name, const char* interfaceId);
    static void        releaseFn(void* ctx, void* link);
    static void        logFn(void* ctx, int level, const char* message);
    static const void* interfaceFn(const rp_host* host, const char* id);

    const DeviceLink*        links_ = nullptr;
    std::size_t              count_ = 0;
    const rp_device_midi_in* midi_ = nullptr;
    Log                      log_ = nullptr;
    rp_host_devices          devices_{this, &acquireFn, &releaseFn};
    rp_host                  host_{RP_ABI_VERSION, this, nullptr, nullptr, &logFn, &interfaceFn};
};

}  // namespace rp::box
````

````cpp
#include "DeviceHost.hpp"

#include <cstring>

namespace rp::box {

void DeviceHost::init(const DeviceLink* links, std::size_t count, const rp_device_midi_in* midi, Log log) {
    links_ = links;
    count_ = links ? count : 0;
    midi_ = midi;
    log_ = log;
}

void* DeviceHost::acquireFn(void* ctx, const char* name, const char* interfaceId) {
    const auto& self = *static_cast<const DeviceHost*>(ctx);
    if (!name || !interfaceId) return nullptr;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < self.count_; ++i) {
        const DeviceLink& l = self.links_[i];
        if (std::strcmp(l.name, name) != 0 || std::strcmp(l.interfaceId, interfaceId) != 0) continue;
        if (l.acquired) l.acquired(l.hookCtx);
        return l.link;
    }
    return nullptr;
}

// Told only for a link this host installed (rp.host.devices/2's identity check): a stray pointer is ignored.
void DeviceHost::releaseFn(void* ctx, void* link) {
    const auto& self = *static_cast<const DeviceHost*>(ctx);
    if (!link) return;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < self.count_; ++i) {
        const DeviceLink& l = self.links_[i];
        if (l.link != link) continue;
        if (l.released) l.released(l.hookCtx);
        return;
    }
}

void DeviceHost::logFn(void* ctx, int level, const char* message) {
    const auto& self = *static_cast<const DeviceHost*>(ctx);
    if (self.log_ && message) self.log_(level, message);
}

const void* DeviceHost::interfaceFn(const rp_host* host, const char* id) {
    const auto& self = *static_cast<const DeviceHost*>(host->ctx);
    if (!id) return nullptr;
    if (std::strcmp(id, RP_HOST_DEVICES_INTERFACE) == 0) return &self.devices_;
    if (std::strcmp(id, RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_INTERFACE) == 0) return self.midi_;
    return nullptr;
}

}  // namespace rp::box
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// A box's plan (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md sections 2 and 5): the blob its build exported from the
// product's plan.json and embedded in the image, loaded at boot into a static arena by the loader
// (graph/PlanLoader.hpp) and run one block a main-loop pass, as the block driver says. Another graph means another
// image (the E3 design's decision 1), so the plan is loaded once and never unloaded.
//
// What it says on the console: the plan it loaded (its nodes, and the arena bytes it takes of the arena's size), or
// why the loader refused it, after which it runs nothing; and a node the executor silences for faulting, once.
//
// Portable (no Pico SDK), so the desktop's tests build it as the box does; the product gives it the line printer.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <span>

#include "BlockDriver.hpp"
#include "graph/PlanLoader.hpp"

namespace rp::box {

class BuiltInPlan {
public:
    // One console line, without its newline.
    using Print = void (*)(const char* line);
    // The most nodes whose faults it tells apart (a fault past them is still counted, and printed without its name).
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kNodes = 64;

    constexpr BuiltInPlan() = default;

    // Loads `blob` (which must outlive the plan: node ids point into it) into `arena`, its nodes created under `host`
    // from `types` (the product's rp_register_packages()). True with the plan's line printed; false with the refusal's.
    bool load(std::span<const std::uint8_t> blob, std::span<std::byte> arena, std::span<const rp_package* const> types,
              const rp_host* host, Print print);
    // One block, when the driver has one due: true when it ran. Nothing without a plan.
    bool run(BlockDriver& driver);

    graph::LoadedPlan*          plan() const { return plan_; }
    const graph::PlanLoadError& error() const { return error_; }

private:
    void printLoaded(std::size_t arenaBytes) const;
    void printRefused() const;
    void reportFaults();

    graph::LoadedPlan*   plan_ = nullptr;
    graph::PlanLoadError error_{};
    Print                print_ = nullptr;
    std::uint32_t        faultsSeen_ = 0;
    bool                 told_[kNodes] = {};
};

}  // namespace rp::box
````
