Create `pico/host/BuiltInPlan.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "BuiltInPlan.hpp"

#include <cstdio>

#include "graph/Executor.hpp"
#include "graph/noinline.hpp"

namespace rp::box {

namespace {

// A NUL-terminated field of the loader's error (each is cut to fit, and terminated).
const char* text(const char* field) { return field[0] ? field : "-"; }

}  // namespace

bool BuiltInPlan::load(std::span<const std::uint8_t> blob, std::span<std::byte> arena,
                       std::span<const rp_package* const> types, const rp_host* host, Print print) {
    print_ = print;
    plan_ = graph::loadPlan(blob, arena, types, host, &error_);
    if (!print_) return plan_ != nullptr;
    if (plan_)
        printLoaded(arena.size());
    else
        printRefused();
    return plan_ != nullptr;
}

// Each line's buffer in a frame of its own, never inlined into load(), so it is not on the stack under the load (the
// deepest chain the box runs, before its interrupts are on).
RP_NOINLINE void BuiltInPlan::printLoaded(std::size_t arenaBytes) const {
    char line[160];
    std::snprintf(line, sizeof line,
                  "[host] plan loaded: %u nodes, %lu of %lu arena bytes, %lu Hz, %lu frames a block",
                  static_cast<unsigned>(plan_->nodes.size()), static_cast<unsigned long>(plan_->bytes),
                  static_cast<unsigned long>(arenaBytes), static_cast<unsigned long>(plan_->sampleRate),
                  static_cast<unsigned long>(plan_->maxFrames));
    print_(line);
    for (const graph::LoadedNode& n : plan_->nodes) {
        std::snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[host]   node %.*s (%s), %lu bytes", static_cast<int>(n.idSize), n.id,
                      n.type->id, static_cast<unsigned long>(n.memoryBytes));
        print_(line);
    }
}

RP_NOINLINE void BuiltInPlan::printRefused() const {
    char line[sizeof error_.code + sizeof error_.node + sizeof error_.message + 64];  // the refusal's, whole
    std::snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[host] the built-in plan was refused: %s %s: %s", text(error_.code),
                  text(error_.node), text(error_.message));
    print_(line);
    print_("[host] no plan runs, and nothing is forwarded");
}

bool BuiltInPlan::run(BlockDriver& driver) {
    if (!plan_) return false;
    std::uint32_t frames = 0;
    rp_transport  transport{};
    if (!driver.next(&frames, &transport)) return false;
    if (frames == 0 || frames > plan_->maxFrames) return false;  // a driver started for another plan: never run it
    graph::runBlock(plan_->view, frames, transport);
    if (plan_->faults.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) != faultsSeen_) reportFaults();
    return true;
}

// The executor bumps the plan's fault count once per node that faults and silences the node from then on; each is
// named here once.
void BuiltInPlan::reportFaults() {
    const std::uint32_t faults = plan_->faults.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    char                line[160];
    std::uint32_t       named = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < plan_->nodes.size(); ++i) {
        const graph::LoadedNode& n = plan_->nodes[i];
        if (!n.faulted.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) continue;
        if (i < kNodes && told_[i]) {
            ++named;
            continue;
        }
        if (i >= kNodes) continue;
        told_[i] = true;
        ++named;
        if (print_) {
            std::snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[host] node %.*s (%s) faulted: the executor silences it from here on",
                          static_cast<int>(n.idSize), n.id, n.type->id);
            print_(line);
        }
    }
    if (named < faults && print_) {
        std::snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[host] %lu more nodes faulted", static_cast<unsigned long>(faults - named));
        print_(line);
    }
    faultsSeen_ = faults;
}

}  // namespace rp::box
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// A box's MIDI UART (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 5): MIDI IN on a hardware UART, read by an interrupt
// into a ring of bytes, each with the microsecond it was taken off the UART, so bytes keep arriving while the main loop
// is blocked in a USB write (about 5 ms each). Polled, a burst overran the UART's 32-byte hardware FIFO in about 10 ms
// and lost some 70% of its bytes. The main loop drains the ring into the staging (MidiStaging), which parses it.
//
// The interrupt is the only writer of the ring's head, the last arrival and the counters: run as the ISR, or by poll()
// with the interrupt masked. The main loop is the only writer of the tail.

#include <cstdint>

#include "MidiStaging.hpp"
#include "hardware/uart.h"

namespace rp::box {

// The ring: one block's worth of bytes, rp.device.midi-in's (RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES), which at the 31250 baud wire
// is 1.3 s of MIDI held while the main loop is busy.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kUartRing = 4096;
static_assert(kUartRing == RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES, "the UART ring holds what rp.device.midi-in takes in a block");

struct UartMidiCounts {
    std::uint32_t rx;        // bytes off the UART
    std::uint32_t overrun;   // bytes lost to a full UART hardware FIFO
    std::uint32_t framing;   // framing / break errors (wiring, or a Type A/B swap)
    std::uint32_t ringFull;  // bytes lost to a full ring
};

// MIDI IN on `uart`'s RX pin `rxPin` at `baud`, 8N1, its interrupt at the lowest priority (it only copies bytes, and
// must never delay PIO-USB's own timer interrupt).
void uartMidiInit(uart_inst_t* uart, unsigned rxPin, unsigned baud);
// Reads what the UART holds now, as the interrupt would: the idle main loop calls it each pass, since a 3-byte message
// is under the receive interrupt's 4-byte threshold and would otherwise wait about 1 ms for the receive timeout.
void uartMidiPoll();
// The ring into the staging, oldest first, until it is empty or the staging refuses a byte (which stays for the next
// pass).
void uartMidiDrain(MidiStaging& staging);
// Drops what the ring holds: stale MIDI, from before the box could forward it.
void uartMidiDiscard();
// When the last byte arrived (the low 32 bits of the microsecond clock).
std::uint32_t uartMidiLastRx();
UartMidiCounts uartMidiCounts();

}  // namespace rp::box
````

Create `pico/host/UartMidi.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "UartMidi.hpp"

#include "hardware/gpio.h"
#include "hardware/irq.h"
#include "hardware/sync.h"
#include "pico/time.h"

namespace rp::box {

namespace {

uart_inst_t*               gUart = nullptr;
std::uint8_t               gRing[kUartRing];
std::uint32_t              gStamp[kUartRing];  // time_us_32() each byte was taken off the UART
volatile std::uint32_t     gHead = 0, gTail = 0;
volatile std::uint32_t     gRx = 0, gOverrun = 0, gFraming = 0, gRingFull = 0;
volatile std::uint32_t     gLastRx = 0;

void onUartIrq() {
    const std::uint32_t now = time_us_32();
    while (uart_is_readable(gUart)) {
        // Read DR whole: bits 8-11 flag this byte's framing / parity / break / overrun.
        const std::uint32_t dr = uart_get_hw(gUart)->dr;
        if (dr & UART_UARTDR_OE_BITS) gOverrun = gOverrun + 1;
        if (dr & (UART_UARTDR_FE_BITS | UART_UARTDR_BE_BITS)) {
            gFraming = gFraming + 1;
            continue;
        }
        const std::uint32_t h = gHead, next = (h + 1) % kUartRing;
        if (next == gTail) {
            gRingFull = gRingFull + 1;
            continue;
        }
        gRing[h] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(dr);
        gStamp[h] = now;
        __dmb();  // the byte is in the ring before the main loop can see the new head
        gHead = next;
        gRx = gRx + 1;
        gLastRx = now;
    }
}

}  // namespace

void uartMidiInit(uart_inst_t* uart, unsigned rxPin, unsigned baud) {
    gUart = uart;
    uart_init(uart, baud);
    gpio_set_function(rxPin, GPIO_FUNC_UART);
    uart_set_format(uart, 8, 1, UART_PARITY_NONE);
    uart_set_fifo_enabled(uart, true);
    irq_set_exclusive_handler(UART_IRQ_NUM(uart), onUartIrq);
    irq_set_priority(UART_IRQ_NUM(uart), PICO_LOWEST_IRQ_PRIORITY);
    irq_set_enabled(UART_IRQ_NUM(uart), true);
    uart_set_irqs_enabled(uart, true, false);
}

void uartMidiPoll() {
    irq_set_enabled(UART_IRQ_NUM(gUart), false);
    onUartIrq();
    irq_set_enabled(UART_IRQ_NUM(gUart), true);
}

void uartMidiDrain(MidiStaging& staging) {
    while (gTail != gHead) {
        const std::uint32_t t = gTail;
        if (!staging.feed(gRing[t], gStamp[t])) return;
        __dmb();  // the byte is read before the interrupt may reuse its slot
        gTail = (t + 1) % kUartRing;
    }
}

void uartMidiDiscard() { gTail = gHead; }

std::uint32_t uartMidiLastRx() { return gLastRx; }

UartMidiCounts uartMidiCounts() { return UartMidiCounts{gRx, gOverrun, gFraming, gRingFull}; }

}  // namespace rp::box
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The box's cart link, its stats and its volume write**

`BoxCartLink` is an `rp::n8::CartLink` over a fixed ring (512 messages and 8 KB, one block's MIDI twice over, in an
all-zero `Storage` in `.bss`): `push` copies and answers false, counted, while not connected (`notReady`) or full
(`full`); `drain(writer, nowMs)` writes the volume first (pending at every connect and on a change; only a failed
write retried, a second later), then the ring in writes of whole messages up to 192 bytes (only a message longer than
192 is split), each timed from its first message's arrival; `releaseNotes` queues note-offs the same way; the last
release puts the volume to -1, as `N8CartLink` does; it keeps a mirror of the node's note books from its own answers,
so a connected note-off for a note the node owed counts as the node's own (`made`). `BoxStats.hpp` is `filtered` in
one function, `handed + tooLong + untaken - (pushes the link received - made)`, exact but in one case only a full link
ring reaches. `CartVolume` writes the volume (`rp::box::writeExpansionVolume`: memWR, then a read-back for the console
line) and answers false only when the transport took nothing; its lines are `written (reads back N)`, `written, but
reads back N`, `written (no read-back)` and, once per failing streak, `expansion volume N: write did not go through,
trying again each second`, which says no `FAILED`, since the gate's `--fail` pattern matches that word.

Create `pico/n8-host/BoxCartLink.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The box's cart link (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md section 5): rp::n8::CartLink (n8/CartLink.hpp) over the
// main loop's one Edio, with no thread of its own. rp.n8.nes pushes into a fixed ring during the block; after the
// block the main loop drains the ring to the cart's FIFO in writes of up to 192 bytes (drain()), so a push never waits
// on the N8, and block work and N8 work never overlap, now and when an audio driver sets the cadence.
//
// - push() copies the message into the ring and answers false, counted, when no game is running (the box's forwarding
//   state, which its N8 part sets each pass through setConnected(): a game is running and the box forwards to it) or
//   when the ring is full.
// - drain() writes whole messages back to back, as many as fit in 192 bytes (a write costs the same ~5 ms whatever it
//   carries, so batching is what lets a burst through), and splits only a message longer than that (a SysEx). A
//   message is counted forwarded, or failed, in the write that carries its last byte.
// - releaseNotes() queues a note-off for each note the same way, behind what was already pushed.
// - setExpansionVolume() records the value (clamped to the register's 0..255, or -1 to leave the register to the
//   cart), and drain() writes it to the cart's config register while connected: at every connect and on a change, as
//   the desktop's N8Host does (and a failed write again a second later). Its -1 (N8Host::EXP_VOL_AUTO) writes nothing
//   here: the desktop's rule for it (unity for an expansion mapper, else the N8 OS's value) is for a link no node
//   holds, which a box with a plan never is, since rp.n8.nes gives its value at its first block.
// - acquire() and release() are the hooks the box installs the link with (rp.host.devices/2), counting the nodes that
//   hold it; the last release puts the volume back to -1, as N8CartLink does.
// - No device jobs: the box offers no rp.host.jobs/1, so rp.n8.nes refuses a job before it reaches the link, and the
//   link's own answer is CartLink's ("not connected").
//
// What it counts is the plan's edge into the cart, which the box's stats read without reaching into the plan: the
// pushes it was handed, and of them the ones rp.n8.nes made itself, the note-offs it owes for notes whose note-off a
// disconnect dropped and pays at the next connected block. The link keeps the node's books on its own answers to tell
// those apart (sounding: a note-on taken, no note-off taken since; owed: a sounding note whose note-off it refused),
// the rules N8Node.cpp's pushMidi keeps, so the box's `filtered` (staged minus what the link was handed from the
// plan's input) stays what the plan dropped. That holds for MIDI pushed through the node's `midi` input, the only input
// the box's plan wires.
//
// Portable (no Pico SDK), so the desktop's tests build it as the box does. One thread: the block and the drain both
// run on the box's main loop, which also sets the connected state.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_device_midi_in.h"
#include "n8/CartLink.hpp"

namespace rp::box {

class BoxCartLink final : public rp::n8::CartLink {
public:
    // Room for one block's MIDI (rp.device.midi-in's queue, which rp.core.midi-filter's matches) twice over, so the
    // note-offs the node owes after a reconnect fit beside a full block: the ring is emptied after every block.
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kMessages = 2 * RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES;
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kBytes = 2 * RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES;
    // The most one FIFO write carries.
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kBatch = 192;
    // How long a failed volume write waits before it is tried again.
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kVolumeRetryMs = 1000;

    // Where the main loop's writes go: the cart's FIFO (`messages` of them end in `data`, and `firstUs` is when the
    // first message it carries arrived), and the cart's expansion-volume register (`again` on a retry of a write that
    // failed). Each answers whether the write reached the cart: a volume written whose read-back differs is written,
    // not retried (the cart's register is its own business from there; N8Host reads nothing back).
    struct Writer {
        void* ctx;
        bool (*fifo)(void* ctx, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t messages,
                     std::uint32_t firstUs);
        bool (*volume)(void* ctx, int value, bool again);
    };
    // When what the plan pushes arrived: `arrival` answers it for a message the block handed the plan at `frame` with
    // these bytes (MidiStaging::arrival), `now` for one the plan made itself. Microseconds, the low 32 bits.
    struct Clock {
        void* ctx;
        std::uint32_t (*now)(void* ctx);
        bool (*arrival)(void* ctx, std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, std::uint32_t* us);
    };

    struct Counts {
        std::uint32_t received = 0;  // pushes, taken or refused
        std::uint32_t made = 0;      // of them, the note-offs rp.n8.nes owed (see above)
        std::uint32_t notReady = 0;  // pushes refused: no game running
        std::uint32_t full = 0;      // pushes refused: the ring full
        std::uint32_t released = 0;  // note-offs releaseNotes queued
        std::uint32_t forwarded = 0; // messages in writes the cart took
        std::uint32_t failed = 0;    // messages in writes that failed
        std::uint32_t sysex = 0;     // of the forwarded, SysEx
        std::uint32_t writes = 0;    // FIFO writes
        std::uint32_t maxBatch = 0;  // the most messages one write carried

        // What the plan handed the link from its input: its pushes, less the node's own note-offs.
        std::uint32_t fromPlanInput() const { return received - made; }
    };

    // The ring and the books, kept apart from the link in a plain struct the box holds in .bss: a polymorphic object
    // is initialised data (its vtable pointer), and what it held inline would be copied out of flash at boot with it.
    struct Message {
        std::uint32_t at;  // arrival, microseconds
        std::uint16_t size;
        bool          sysex;
    };
    struct Storage {
        std::uint8_t      bytes[kBytes];
        Message           messages[kMessages];
        std::uint8_t      batch[kBatch];
        rp::n8::CartNotes sounding, owed;
    };

    constexpr explicit BoxCartLink(Storage& storage) : s_(storage) {}
    void setClock(const Clock& clock) { clock_ = clock; }

    // rp::n8::CartLink.
    bool push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush,
              double sampleRate) override;
    bool          connected() const override { return connected_; }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return std::uint64_t{counts_.notReady} + counts_.full; }
    void          setExpansionVolume(int value) override;
    void          releaseNotes(const rp::n8::CartNotes& notes) override;

    // The box's side. Whether a game is running and the box forwards to it: a connect has the volume written again,
    // and a disconnect drops what is queued (counted not ready), as nothing may reach a cart that went away.
    void setConnected(bool connected);
    // The volume while connected, then the ring, in writes of up to kBatch bytes, until it is empty.
    void drain(const Writer& writer, std::uint32_t nowMs);
    void acquire() { ++holders_; }
    void release();

    const Counts& counts() const { return counts_; }
    int           expansionVolume() const { return volume_; }
    std::uint32_t queued() const { return messageCount_; }
    int           holders() const { return holders_; }

private:
    bool enqueue(const std::uint8_t* data, std::uint32_t size, std::uint32_t at);
    void book(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool taken);
    void discard();

    Storage& s_;
    Clock    clock_{};
    bool     connected_ = false;

    // The ring (s_.bytes and s_.messages): messages and their bytes, each in a circle of its own.
    std::uint32_t byteHead_ = 0, byteCount_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t messageHead_ = 0, messageCount_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t frontSent_ = 0;  // the bytes of the oldest message already written (a split one)

    int           volume_ = -1;
    bool          volumePending_ = false;
    bool          volumeWaiting_ = false;  // a failed write waits until retryAtMs_
    std::uint32_t retryAtMs_ = 0;
    int           holders_ = 0;

    Counts counts_{};
};

}  // namespace rp::box
````

````cpp
#include "BoxCartLink.hpp"

namespace rp::box {

using rp::n8::NoteEvent;
using rp::n8::noteEvent;

bool BoxCartLink::push(std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool flush,
                       double sampleRate) {
    // The flush flag is the bytes port's barrier, which a FIFO written in order keeps by itself, and the frame and the
    // rate place nothing on a link that writes after the block: the frame only finds when the message arrived.
    (void)flush;
    (void)sampleRate;
    if (size == 0) return true;  // nothing to lose
    ++counts_.received;
    const NoteEvent note = noteEvent(data, size);
    if (connected_ && note.off && s_.owed.test(note.index)) ++counts_.made;
    bool taken = false;
    if (!connected_) {
        ++counts_.notReady;
    } else {
        std::uint32_t at = 0;
        if (!clock_.arrival || !clock_.arrival(clock_.ctx, frame, data, size, &at))
            at = clock_.now ? clock_.now(clock_.ctx) : 0;
        taken = size <= kBytes && enqueue(data, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size), at);
        if (!taken) ++counts_.full;
    }
    book(data, size, taken);
    return taken;
}

// The node's books on its notes, kept from this link's own answers (N8Node.cpp's pushMidi and payOwed).
void BoxCartLink::book(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size, bool taken) {
    const NoteEvent note = noteEvent(data, size);
    if (note.on && taken) {
        s_.sounding.set(note.index);
        s_.owed.reset(note.index);
    } else if (note.off) {
        if (taken) {
            s_.sounding.reset(note.index);
            s_.owed.reset(note.index);
        } else if (s_.sounding.test(note.index)) {
            s_.owed.set(note.index);
        }
    }
}

bool BoxCartLink::enqueue(const std::uint8_t* data, std::uint32_t size, std::uint32_t at) {
    if (messageCount_ == kMessages || size > kBytes - byteCount_) return false;
    std::uint32_t write = (byteHead_ + byteCount_) % kBytes;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) {
        s_.bytes[write] = data[i];
        write = write + 1 == kBytes ? 0 : write + 1;
    }
    byteCount_ += size;
    s_.messages[(messageHead_ + messageCount_) % kMessages] =
        Message{at, static_cast<std::uint16_t>(size), data[0] == 0xF0};
    ++messageCount_;
    return true;
}

void BoxCartLink::releaseNotes(const rp::n8::CartNotes& notes) {
    const std::uint32_t at = clock_.now ? clock_.now(clock_.ctx) : 0;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < notes.size(); ++i) {
        if (!notes.test(i)) continue;
        s_.sounding.reset(i);
        s_.owed.reset(i);
        const std::uint8_t off[3] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x80 | (i / 128)), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i % 128),
                                     0};
        if (!connected_)
            ++counts_.notReady;
        else if (!enqueue(off, sizeof off, at))
            ++counts_.full;
        else
            ++counts_.released;
    }
}

void BoxCartLink::setExpansionVolume(int value) {
    const int clamped = value < 0 ? -1 : (value > 255 ? 255 : value);
    if (clamped == volume_) return;
    volume_ = clamped;
    volumePending_ = true;
    volumeWaiting_ = false;
}

void BoxCartLink::release() {
    if (holders_ > 0 && --holders_ == 0) {
        volume_ = -1;
        volumePending_ = false;
    }
}

void BoxCartLink::setConnected(bool connected) {
    if (connected && !connected_) {
        volumePending_ = true;  // every connect again: a fresh game's register is the N8 OS's
        volumeWaiting_ = false;
    }
    if (!connected && connected_) discard();
    connected_ = connected;
}

void BoxCartLink::discard() {
    counts_.notReady += messageCount_;
    byteHead_ = byteCount_ = messageHead_ = messageCount_ = frontSent_ = 0;
}

void BoxCartLink::drain(const Writer& writer, std::uint32_t nowMs) {
    if (connected_ && volumePending_ && (!volumeWaiting_ || static_cast<std::int32_t>(nowMs - retryAtMs_) >= 0)) {
        if (volume_ < 0 || (writer.volume && writer.volume(writer.ctx, volume_, volumeWaiting_))) {
            volumePending_ = volumeWaiting_ = false;
        } else {
            volumeWaiting_ = true;
            retryAtMs_ = nowMs + kVolumeRetryMs;
        }
    }
    while (messageCount_ != 0) {
        // One write: the messages that fit whole, from the oldest; one longer than a write is split across writes.
        std::uint32_t length = 0, carried = 0, sysex = 0;
        const std::uint32_t firstUs = s_.messages[messageHead_].at;
        while (messageCount_ != 0 && length < kBatch) {
            const Message&      m = s_.messages[messageHead_];
            const std::uint32_t left = m.size - frontSent_;
            if (frontSent_ == 0 && m.size <= kBatch && length + m.size > kBatch) break;  // whole, in the next write
            const std::uint32_t take = left < kBatch - length ? left : kBatch - length;
            for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < take; ++i) {
                s_.batch[length++] = s_.bytes[byteHead_];
                byteHead_ = byteHead_ + 1 == kBytes ? 0 : byteHead_ + 1;
            }
            byteCount_ -= take;
            frontSent_ += take;
            if (frontSent_ < m.size) break;  // the rest of it goes in the next write
            ++carried;
            if (m.sysex) ++sysex;
            frontSent_ = 0;
            messageHead_ = messageHead_ + 1 == kMessages ? 0 : messageHead_ + 1;
            --messageCount_;
        }
        const bool ok = writer.fifo && writer.fifo(writer.ctx, s_.batch, length, carried, firstUs);
        ++counts_.writes;
        if (ok) {
            counts_.forwarded += carried;
            counts_.sysex += sysex;
        } else {
            counts_.failed += carried;
        }
        if (carried > counts_.maxBatch) counts_.maxBatch = carried;
    }
}

}  // namespace rp::box
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The box's `filtered` count (main.cpp's [stats]), from the plan's two edges, which the host owns: what the staging
// dropped before the plan (a SysEx past 4 KB, staged messages no block took) and what the plan took and did not hand
// the cart link from its input (what its filter dropped, and rp.device.midi-in's own overflow). One function, so the
// desktop's test holds the firmware's arithmetic rather than a copy of it.
//
// Exact but in one case, which only a full link ring (`linkfull=` moving) reaches: when rp.n8.nes's payment of an
// owed note-off is refused for room and the block's input carries the note-off for that note, the link counts the
// input's push as the node's own (`made`), so `filtered` reads one high.

#include <cstdint>

#include "BoxCartLink.hpp"
#include "MidiStaging.hpp"

namespace rp::box {

inline std::uint32_t filtered(const MidiStaging::Counts& in, const BoxCartLink::Counts& out) {
    const std::int64_t dropped = std::int64_t{in.handed} + in.tooLong + in.untaken - out.fromPlanInput();
    return dropped > 0 ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(dropped) : 0;
}

}  // namespace rp::box
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The box's expansion-volume write (BoxCartLink's Writer::volume): rp.n8.nes's value to the N8's FPGA master volume
// for the expansion audio (VRC6 / VRC7 / N163 / Sunsoft 5B / MMC5; at 0 every expansion voice is silent), written over
// the box's Edio and read back (a live register) for the console line. The rule: only a write the transport failed
// (memWR not ok) answers false, so the link tries it again a second later, and says so once (not on a retry,
// `again`); a write that went through is done whatever it reads back, as N8Host takes a write that went through, and
// says which of three it came to: `written (reads back N)`, `written, but reads back N`, `written (no read-back)`.
// The failure's line says `did not go through`, never `FAILED`: the hardware gate's boot legs stop on that word
// (pico/n8-host/loop.sh --fail "no 'k'|FAILED", tested before the boot's own line), and a transient failure here is
// retried, not a failed boot. Portable, so the desktop's test drives the outcomes over a fake transport.

#include "n8/Edio.hpp"

namespace rp::box {

// One console line, without its newline.
using VolumePrint = void (*)(const char* line);

bool writeExpansionVolume(rp::n8::Edio& edio, int value, bool again, VolumePrint print);

}  // namespace rp::box
````

````cpp
#include "CartVolume.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>

namespace rp::box {

bool writeExpansionVolume(rp::n8::Edio& edio, int value, bool again, VolumePrint print) {
    char               line[128];
    const std::uint8_t v = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(value);
    if (!edio.memWR(rp::n8::Edio::ADDR_EXP_VOL, &v, 1).ok()) {
        if (!again && print) {
            std::snprintf(line, sizeof line,
                          "[n8-host] cart link: expansion volume %d: write did not go through, "
                          "trying again each second",
                          value);
            print(line);
        }
        return false;
    }
    std::uint8_t back = 0;
    if (!edio.memRD(rp::n8::Edio::ADDR_EXP_VOL, &back, 1).ok())
        std::snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[n8-host] cart link: expansion volume %d written (no read-back)", value);
    else if (back != v)
        std::snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[n8-host] cart link: expansion volume %d written, but reads back %u", value,
                      static_cast<unsigned>(back));
    else
        std::snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[n8-host] cart link: expansion volume %d written (reads back %u)", value,
                      static_cast<unsigned>(back));
    if (print) print(line);
    return true;
}

}  // namespace rp::box
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The built-in plan and the main loop**

`plan.json` is the bridge: `rp.device.midi-in` -> `rp.core.midi-filter` dropping `polyAftertouch`,
`channelAftertouch`, `systemCommon` and `realtime` (what the bridge never forwarded: the old firmware passed channel
voice and SysEx only, and stress.sh's runstat case expects real time gone) -> `rp.n8.nes`; `plan.cmake` holds it,
48000 Hz, 256 frames and the 131072-byte arena in one place for the firmware and the tests. `main.cpp` keeps every N8
flow byte for byte (the probe, the menu boot, box.cfg, health, recovery, the SysEx pick, every TinyUSB callback) and
gains the statics (the arena, the staging, the driver, the host, the plan, the link), the writers (`fifo_write`, E2's
batch flush with its acknowledgement timing; `volume_write`, forwarding to `CartVolume`), the box's SysEx hook,
`[stats]` from the two edges (`linkfull=` and `skipped=` trailing, every other field's name kept), and the pass in the
design's order: watchdog and USB; poll and drain the UART into the staging; run the block and end it (or, with no
plan, clear the staging); drain the link; the N8 part with the stale-MIDI discard at the forward edge and the link's
connected state; stats. `midi_to_fifo`, the SysEx emitters, the batch buffer, `exp_vol_check` and `expansion_chip` go.
`LatTrace.hpp` is the latency trace `-DN8_LAT_TRACE=1` builds (a message's way from its UART stamp to the N8's
acknowledgement and each segment of a pass, in microseconds, cycles and XIP misses; its `LAT()` hooks are `((void)0)`
otherwise). `CMakeLists.txt`: `device-image.cmake` before the packages (node-sdk, graph-runtime, core, device-io, n8);
`host.cmake` and `plan.cmake`; `RP_EXPORT_PLAN_TOOL` (a cache path, default `build/`'s exporter; the configure refuses
a missing one, saying how to build it) and the custom command exporting `plan.json` with `--arena 131072 --sample-rate
48000 --max-frames 256 --header kBuiltInPlan` into the build dir's `generated/n8_host_plan.hpp`;
`pico_set_binary_type(n8_host copy_to_ram)` with the why and the rig's figures; the stack's chains;
`PICO_HEAP_SIZE=0`; `retroplug_product(n8-host DEVICE PACKAGES core device-io n8 TARGETS n8_host)`; the `N8_EXP_VOL`
knob retired (the volume is the node's param) and `N8_LAT_TRACE` added. `SofTimer.cpp`'s comment: the 64-bit timer
read is in RAM now too. `UsbCdcTransport.cpp`'s pragma is GCC's alone, since the desktop test compiles it with other
compilers. `loop.sh` takes the desktop build's exporter (`RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR`, default `build/`) and passes it to
the configure, pointing an existing build dir at it when its cache names another; it builds no desktop tree itself,
and refuses with how to build the exporter when it is missing.

````cmake
# The box's built-in plan (docs/modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md sections 2 and 5): plan.json beside this file, and
# what it is exported for. Included by the firmware's CMakeLists.txt, which exports it at build time with
# retroplug-export-plan and embeds the blob, and by the desktop's tests (packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake), whose
# golden pins the blob these give, so a change to the format, a node's settings or one of these is a reviewed diff.
#
# plan.json is the bridge, MIDI in to the cart: rp.device.midi-in (the MIDI the box parses and stages, every message
# as it came), rp.core.midi-filter dropping what BlipToaster's FIFO is not fed (poly aftertouch and channel pressure,
# high-rate streams a Launchpad floods and no ROM here reads, and system common and real time, which the bridge never
# forwarded), and rp.n8.nes, the cart. A graph document takes no comment, so the why is here.
#
# The rate and block are the design's: 48 kHz and 256 frames (5.3 ms). The arena is the image's static arena, which
# the plan must fit at export (and which the loader holds it to at boot): 128 KiB. The bridge takes under a quarter of
# it; the rest is room for a later plan's audio, whose buffers are 1 KiB a channel at 256 frames (main.cpp).
include_guard(GLOBAL)
set(N8_HOST_PLAN "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/plan.json")
set(N8_HOST_PLAN_SAMPLE_RATE 48000)
set(N8_HOST_PLAN_MAX_FRAMES 256)
set(N8_HOST_ARENA_BYTES 131072)
````

Create `pico/n8-host/LatTrace.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once
// The latency trace (-DN8_LAT_TRACE=1, a measurement build: main.cpp includes this only then, and the default image
// holds none of it). It times one isolated message's way through the box, the main loop's passes and what each part
// of a pass costs, and prints a summary on two lines of their own once MIDI has been quiet for a second, a message has
// been timed since the last summary and no timed write is waiting for its acknowledgement:
//
//   [lat] msgs n=<N> us avg/max: rx>drain a/m drain>block a/m block>push a/m push>write a/m write a/m write>ack a/m
//         total a/m over1500=<k> | path <cycles> cyc <misses> miss, block <cycles> cyc <misses> miss,
//         write <misses> miss
//   [lat] passes idle n=<N> <us> us avg, <us> max, <misses> miss avg, <misses> max | block in <p>% of passes,
//         <us> us avg, <us> max | busy <N> | seg max us usb .. stats .. | worst msg <us>: rx in <seg>, ack in <seg>
//
// The message's points: its last byte's UART timestamp (the poll's, or the RX interrupt's), the end of the drain that
// took it into the staging, the start of the block that pushed it, the link's push (BoxCartLink asking the staging when
// it arrived), the FIFO write issued and returned, and the N8's acknowledgement (tuh_cdc_tx_complete_cb). Each is
// timed on the microsecond clock; the message's own processing (from its pass's UART poll to the write) is also
// counted in core cycles (the M33's DWT cycle counter) and in XIP cache misses (the XIP block's hit and access
// counters, read at each point), which is what tells running work from waiting on flash. The image runs from SRAM
// (CMakeLists.txt), so they read 0 unless something it runs is in flash; run from flash, a miss cost about 90 cycles
// on the rig, and an isolated message about 90 of them.
//
// The messages timed are the writes main.cpp's `lat=` times (the oldest write not yet acknowledged), less one led by
// no UART message (a note-off rp.n8.nes owed, which the link timed from now); for isolated messages `total` is `lat=`.
// A pass counts as the one that drained a message when the UART's byte count rose since the last drain, which is the
// interrupt's count of bytes into the ring: a byte the interrupt takes in the few instructions between the drain and
// that read, or one the staging refused and left in the ring, marks the wrong pass, and its write, which then has no
// drain before it, is left out rather than mistimed.
//
// A pass is cut into segments (usb: the watchdog and tuh_task; uart: the poll and drain; block: the plan's block and
// the staging's end; link: the cart link's drain and its writes; n8: the probe, boot and connect edge; diag: sniff and
// health; watch: link_watch and the LED; stats: stats_report and its line), each timed. An idle pass is one that took
// no byte, wrote nothing and ran under 1 ms (no USB transfer, no console line); the rest are busy. `rx in <seg>` names
// the segment the worst message's last byte arrived in, so a byte the RX interrupt took while a console line or a USB
// read held the loop says which; `ack in <seg>` names where its acknowledgement was seen (usb: the pass's own
// tuh_task, or inside an Edio wait). A byte that arrived while the trace printed its own summary is `rx in report`.
//
// Its own cost: about 400 instructions a pass (counted in an emulator; an idle pass is about 480 without it), so a
// trace build's latency reads a few microseconds above the plain image's. It also changes the loop's block cadence: on
// the rig a traced idle pass took about 21 us, a block included, past the 20.8 us a frame lasts at 48 kHz, so a traced
// image runs a block in nearly every pass where the plain image runs one in about three, and `drain>block` reads 0
// where the plain image can wait up to a frame for its block. The summary itself goes through the SDK's console, which
// waits for the UART: its two lines of about 300 characters hold the loop about 56 ms, and a message that arrives
// meanwhile waits for them (`rx in report`).
//
// The counter arithmetic as it stands (separate access and hit totals, every difference through since()) has run in an
// emulator only: the rig figures above came from an earlier build of this trace, whose miss and write fields could
// wrap (a hit read after its access, an acknowledgement that came inside fifoWR).

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>

#include <initializer_list>

#include "hardware/clocks.h"
#include "hardware/structs/m33.h"
#include "hardware/structs/qmi.h"
#include "hardware/structs/xip_ctrl.h"
#include "pico/time.h"

namespace lat {

enum Seg : uint8_t { Usb, Uart, Block, Link, N8, Diag, Watch, Stats, kSegs };
// The segments' names, then kSegs's ("-": before the timelines kept) and kReport's (while the summary printed).
inline constexpr uint8_t kReport = kSegs + 1;
inline const char* const kSegNames[kSegs + 2] = {"usb",   "uart", "block", "link", "n8",
                                                 "diag",  "watch", "stats", "-",   "report"};

// A moment: the microsecond clock, the cycle counter and the XIP block's access and hit counts (running totals).
struct Point {
    uint32_t us, cyc, acc, hit;
};

// What passed between two moments. Each figure is a free-running 32-bit count, so a difference is taken modulo 2^32,
// and one that comes out negative (a later read that raced an earlier one by a count or two) is 0, never a wrap.
inline uint32_t since(uint32_t from, uint32_t to) {
    return static_cast<int32_t>(to - from) < 0 ? 0u : to - from;
}
// XIP accesses the cache did not serve between two moments: the accesses less the hits, at least 0.
inline uint32_t missesBetween(const Point& a, const Point& b) {
    const uint32_t acc = b.acc - a.acc, hit = b.hit - a.hit;
    return acc > hit ? acc - hit : 0u;
}

struct Acc {
    uint64_t sum = 0;
    uint32_t max = 0, n = 0;
    void add(uint32_t v) {
        sum += v;
        if (v > max) max = v;
        ++n;
    }
    uint32_t avg() const { return n ? static_cast<uint32_t>(sum / n) : 0; }
    void reset() { *this = Acc{}; }
};

struct State {
    uint32_t cycPerUs = 120;
    bool     cyccnt = false;
    // The XIP counters, folded each pass into running totals and cleared, so neither saturates.
    uint32_t accBase = 0, hitBase = 0;
    // This pass's segment starts, and the last pass's (a byte the RX interrupt took arrived in one of those).
    Point    seg[kSegs + 1] = {};
    uint32_t prevSegUs[kSegs + 1] = {};
    uint32_t reportFrom = 0, reportTo = 0;  // when the last summary was printing (its lines hold the loop)
    uint8_t  cur = Usb;
    uint32_t rxAtDrain = 0;   // the UART's byte count at the last drain
    uint64_t blocksAtPass = 0;
    bool     tookBytes = false, wrote = false, blockRan = false;
    // The last drain that took bytes: when it ended, its pass's poll (the processing's start) and the segment timeline
    // the bytes arrived in (that pass's and the one before).
    Point    drainStart{}, drainEnd{};
    uint32_t drainSegUs[kSegs + 1] = {}, drainPrevSegUs[kSegs + 1] = {};
    // The pushes of the current block, for the write to find its first message's.
    static constexpr int kPushes = 8;
    struct Push {
        uint32_t stamp, us;
    } push[kPushes] = {};
    int      pushes = 0;
    Point    blockStart{};
    uint32_t blockCyc = 0, blockMiss = 0;  // the pass's block: its cycles and misses, kept for the write
    Point    writeStart{};
    // The write being timed (the one tuh_cdc_tx_complete_cb will acknowledge), and the message it carries first.
    bool     armed = false;
    bool     returned = false;  // the write's fifoWR call has returned (its acknowledgement can come first)
    uint32_t stamp = 0, drainUs = 0, blockAt = 0, pushAt = 0, writeAt = 0, writeRet = 0, pathCyc = 0, pathMiss = 0,
             writeMiss = 0, msgBlockCyc = 0, msgBlockMiss = 0;
    uint8_t  rxSeg = kSegs;
    // What the summary reports, since the last one.
    Acc rxDrain, drainBlock, blockPush, pushWrite, write, writeAck, total, path, pathMisses, msgBlock, msgBlockMisses,
        writeMisses, idleUs10, idleMiss, blockUs10;
    uint32_t over1500 = 0, passes = 0, blockPasses = 0, busy = 0;
    uint32_t segMax[kSegs] = {};
    uint32_t worstTotal = 0;
    uint8_t  worstRxSeg = kSegs, worstAckSeg = kSegs;
};
inline State g;

inline uint32_t cycles() { return g.cyccnt ? m33_hw->dwt_cyccnt : time_us_32() * g.cycPerUs; }
// The hits are read before the accesses, so that the accesses a moment counts always cover its hits.
inline Point now() {
    const uint32_t us = time_us_32(), cyc = cycles(), hit = g.hitBase + xip_ctrl_hw->ctr_hit;
    return Point{us, cyc, g.accBase + xip_ctrl_hw->ctr_acc, hit};
}

inline void init() {
    g.cycPerUs = clock_get_hz(clk_sys) / 1000000u;
    m33_hw->demcr |= M33_DEMCR_TRCENA_BITS;
    // The cycle counter is optional in an M33 (DWT_CTRL.NOCYCCNT, bit 25, says it is absent): the microsecond clock
    // stands in for it then, at a microsecond's resolution.
    g.cyccnt = (m33_hw->dwt_ctrl & (1u << 25)) == 0;
    if (g.cyccnt) {
        m33_hw->dwt_cyccnt = 0;
        m33_hw->dwt_ctrl |= M33_DWT_CTRL_CYCCNTENA_BITS;
    }
    xip_ctrl_hw->ctr_acc = 0;
    xip_ctrl_hw->ctr_hit = 0;
    // What one XIP miss costs follows from the flash interface's set-up: the clock divider (TIMING bits 7:0), the read
    // format and command the boot left in QMI window 0.
    printf("[lat] trace on: clk_sys %lu MHz, cycle counter %s, qmi m0 timing 0x%08lx (clkdiv %lu) rfmt 0x%08lx rcmd "
           "0x%08lx, xip ctrl 0x%08lx\n",
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.cycPerUs), g.cyccnt ? "on" : "absent (us clock)",
           static_cast<unsigned long>(qmi_hw->m[0].timing), static_cast<unsigned long>(qmi_hw->m[0].timing & 0xffu),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(qmi_hw->m[0].rfmt), static_cast<unsigned long>(qmi_hw->m[0].rcmd),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(xip_ctrl_hw->ctrl));
}

inline void mark(Seg s) {
    g.seg[s] = now();
    g.cur = s;
}

inline void passBegin() {
    // Fold the XIP counters into the running totals and clear them, so that a pass never sees one saturate.
    g.hitBase += xip_ctrl_hw->ctr_hit;
    xip_ctrl_hw->ctr_hit = 0;
    g.accBase += xip_ctrl_hw->ctr_acc;
    xip_ctrl_hw->ctr_acc = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i <= kSegs; ++i) g.prevSegUs[i] = g.seg[i].us;
    g.tookBytes = g.wrote = g.blockRan = false;
    mark(Usb);
}

// After the UART's drain: the block segment starts. `rx` is the UART's byte count; any rise since the last drain is
// taken as bytes this drain took into the staging (the header says when it is not).
inline void drained(uint32_t rx, uint64_t blocks) {
    mark(Block);
    g.blocksAtPass = blocks;
    g.pushes = 0;
    g.blockStart = g.seg[Block];
    if (rx != g.rxAtDrain) {
        g.rxAtDrain = rx;
        g.tookBytes = true;
        g.drainStart = g.seg[Uart];
        g.drainEnd = g.seg[Block];
        // This pass's segments up to the drain (the later ones have not started), and the whole pass before.
        for (int i = 0; i <= kSegs; ++i) {
            g.drainSegUs[i] = i <= Block ? g.seg[i].us : 0;
            g.drainPrevSegUs[i] = g.prevSegUs[i];
        }
    }
}

// After the block and the staging's end: the link segment starts.
inline void blockDone(uint64_t blocks) {
    mark(Link);
    g.blockRan = blocks != g.blocksAtPass;
    if (g.blockRan) {
        g.blockCyc = since(g.blockStart.cyc, g.seg[Link].cyc);
        g.blockMiss = missesBetween(g.blockStart, g.seg[Link]);
    }
}

// The link asked when a message it was pushed arrived, and was told `stamp`.
inline void pushed(uint32_t stamp) {
    if (g.pushes < State::kPushes) g.push[g.pushes++] = State::Push{stamp, time_us_32()};
}

// Which segment a moment fell in: kReport while the last summary printed, else on the drain's own pass or the one
// before; kSegs when earlier than both.
inline uint8_t segOf(uint32_t us) {
    if (g.reportTo != 0 && static_cast<int32_t>(us - g.reportFrom) >= 0 && static_cast<int32_t>(g.reportTo - us) >= 0)
        return kReport;
    for (int i = kSegs - 1; i >= 0; --i)
        if (static_cast<int32_t>(us - g.drainSegUs[i]) >= 0 && g.drainSegUs[i] != 0) return static_cast<uint8_t>(i);
    for (int i = kSegs - 1; i >= 0; --i)
        if (static_cast<int32_t>(us - g.drainPrevSegUs[i]) >= 0 && g.drainPrevSegUs[i] != 0)
            return static_cast<uint8_t>(i);
    return kSegs;
}

// A FIFO write is issued, carrying first the message that arrived at `firstUs`; `timed` when it is the write the
// acknowledgement will time (main.cpp arms ack_from_us only while no other write is pending).
inline void writeBegin(uint32_t firstUs, bool timed) {
    g.wrote = true;
    // A write the acknowledgement does not time leaves the one it does armed: main.cpp times the oldest.
    if (!timed) return;
    // Only a write led by a message off the UART: one the link timed from now (a note-off rp.n8.nes owed, which never
    // arrived) is no UART message, and has no drain before it. The acknowledgement then times this write, so nothing
    // is armed.
    if (static_cast<int32_t>(g.drainEnd.us - firstUs) < 0) {
        g.armed = false;
        return;
    }
    const Point p = now();
    g.armed = true;
    g.stamp = firstUs;
    g.drainUs = g.drainEnd.us;
    g.blockAt = g.blockStart.us;
    g.pushAt = p.us;
    for (int i = 0; i < g.pushes; ++i)
        if (g.push[i].stamp == firstUs) {
            g.pushAt = g.push[i].us;
            break;
        }
    g.writeAt = p.us;
    g.pathCyc = since(g.drainStart.cyc, p.cyc);
    g.pathMiss = missesBetween(g.drainStart, p);
    g.writeStart = p;
    g.returned = false;
    g.msgBlockCyc = g.blockCyc;
    g.msgBlockMiss = g.blockMiss;
    g.rxSeg = segOf(firstUs);
}

inline void writeEnd(bool ok) {
    if (!g.armed) return;
    if (!ok) {
        g.armed = false;
        return;
    }
    if (g.returned) return;  // acknowledged inside the call (acked)
    const Point p = now();
    g.returned = true;
    g.writeRet = p.us;
    g.writeMiss = missesBetween(g.writeStart, p);
}

// The N8 acknowledged the timed write (main.cpp's tuh_cdc_tx_complete_cb, on the same arming).
inline void acked() {
    if (!g.armed) return;
    g.armed = false;
    // fifoWR pumps tuh_task, so the acknowledgement can come before the call returns: the write then lasted until it.
    const Point t = now();
    if (!g.returned) {
        g.returned = true;
        g.writeRet = t.us;
        g.writeMiss = missesBetween(g.writeStart, t);
    }
    const uint32_t total = since(g.stamp, t.us);
    g.rxDrain.add(since(g.stamp, g.drainUs));
    g.drainBlock.add(since(g.drainUs, g.blockAt));
    g.blockPush.add(since(g.blockAt, g.pushAt));
    g.pushWrite.add(since(g.pushAt, g.writeAt));
    g.write.add(since(g.writeAt, g.writeRet));
    g.writeAck.add(since(g.writeRet, t.us));
    g.total.add(total);
    g.path.add(g.pathCyc);
    g.pathMisses.add(g.pathMiss);
    g.msgBlock.add(g.msgBlockCyc);
    g.msgBlockMisses.add(g.msgBlockMiss);
    g.writeMisses.add(g.writeMiss);
    if (total > 1500) ++g.over1500;
    if (total > g.worstTotal) {
        g.worstTotal = total;
        g.worstRxSeg = g.rxSeg;
        g.worstAckSeg = g.cur;
    }
}

// Formats and prints the summary: called from passEnd, after a second of quiet. Out of line, as passEnd is, so that
// neither its fields nor passEnd's bookkeeping sit in main's frame.
static void __noinline report();

static void __noinline passEnd(uint32_t lastRxUs) {
    const Point end = now();
    g.seg[kSegs] = end;
    uint32_t       longest = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < kSegs; ++i) {
        const uint32_t d = since(g.seg[i].us, g.seg[i + 1].us);
        if (d > g.segMax[i]) g.segMax[i] = d;
        if (d > longest) longest = d;
    }
    const uint32_t passUs = since(g.seg[Usb].us, end.us);
    ++g.passes;
    if (g.blockRan) {
        ++g.blockPasses;
        g.blockUs10.add(g.blockCyc * 10u / g.cycPerUs);
    }
    if (!g.tookBytes && !g.wrote && passUs < 1000) {
        // Tenths of a microsecond from the cycle counter: an idle pass is a few microseconds.
        g.idleUs10.add(since(g.seg[Usb].cyc, end.cyc) * 10u / g.cycPerUs);
        g.idleMiss.add(missesBetween(g.seg[Usb], end));
    } else {
        ++g.busy;
    }
    if (g.total.n != 0 && !g.armed && since(lastRxUs, end.us) > 1000000u) report();
}

static void __noinline report() {
    g.reportFrom = time_us_32();
    const auto am = [](const Acc& a, char* out, size_t cap) {
        snprintf(out, cap, "%lu/%lu", static_cast<unsigned long>(a.avg()), static_cast<unsigned long>(a.max));
    };
    char f[12][24];
    am(g.rxDrain, f[0], sizeof f[0]);
    am(g.drainBlock, f[1], sizeof f[1]);
    am(g.blockPush, f[2], sizeof f[2]);
    am(g.pushWrite, f[3], sizeof f[3]);
    am(g.write, f[4], sizeof f[4]);
    am(g.writeAck, f[5], sizeof f[5]);
    am(g.total, f[6], sizeof f[6]);
    am(g.path, f[7], sizeof f[7]);
    am(g.pathMisses, f[8], sizeof f[8]);
    am(g.msgBlock, f[9], sizeof f[9]);
    am(g.msgBlockMisses, f[10], sizeof f[10]);
    am(g.writeMisses, f[11], sizeof f[11]);
    printf("[lat] msgs n=%lu us avg/max: rx>drain %s drain>block %s block>push %s push>write %s write %s write>ack %s "
           "total %s over1500=%lu | path %s cyc %s miss, block %s cyc %s miss, write %s miss\n",
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.total.n), f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3], f[4], f[5], f[6],
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.over1500), f[7], f[8], f[9], f[10], f[11]);
    const uint32_t idle = g.idleUs10.avg(), idleMax = g.idleUs10.max, blk = g.blockUs10.avg(), blkMax = g.blockUs10.max;
    printf("[lat] passes idle n=%lu %lu.%lu us avg, %lu.%lu max, %lu miss avg, %lu max | block in %lu%% of passes, "
           "%lu.%lu us avg, %lu.%lu max | busy %lu | seg max us usb %lu uart %lu block %lu link %lu n8 %lu diag %lu "
           "watch %lu stats %lu | worst msg %lu: rx in %s, ack in %s\n",
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.idleUs10.n), static_cast<unsigned long>(idle / 10),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(idle % 10), static_cast<unsigned long>(idleMax / 10),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(idleMax % 10), static_cast<unsigned long>(g.idleMiss.avg()),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.idleMiss.max),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.passes ? static_cast<uint64_t>(g.blockPasses) * 100u / g.passes : 0),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(blk / 10), static_cast<unsigned long>(blk % 10),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(blkMax / 10), static_cast<unsigned long>(blkMax % 10),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.busy), static_cast<unsigned long>(g.segMax[Usb]),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.segMax[Uart]), static_cast<unsigned long>(g.segMax[Block]),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.segMax[Link]), static_cast<unsigned long>(g.segMax[N8]),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.segMax[Diag]), static_cast<unsigned long>(g.segMax[Watch]),
           static_cast<unsigned long>(g.segMax[Stats]), static_cast<unsigned long>(g.worstTotal),
           kSegNames[g.worstRxSeg], kSegNames[g.worstAckSeg]);
    g.reportTo = time_us_32();
    // A fresh window: the counters only (the clock set-up, the XIP totals and the timelines carry on).
    for (Acc* a : {&g.rxDrain, &g.drainBlock, &g.blockPush, &g.pushWrite, &g.write, &g.writeAck, &g.total, &g.path,
                   &g.pathMisses, &g.msgBlock, &g.msgBlockMisses, &g.writeMisses, &g.idleUs10, &g.idleMiss,
                   &g.blockUs10})
        a->reset();
    g.over1500 = g.passes = g.blockPasses = g.busy = 0;
    for (uint32_t& m : g.segMax) m = 0;
    g.worstTotal = 0;
    g.worstRxSeg = g.worstAckSeg = kSegs;
}

}  // namespace lat
````

````diff
-# A 4 KB main stack: all of SCRATCH_Y, which holds nothing else. The box's deepest chain (the main loop, a boot through
-# bootRom and box.cfg's save, a transport wait, TinyUSB's callbacks and printf, with the UART and SOF interrupts
-# nested on top) comes to about 2.3 KB summed pessimistically, past the SDK's 2 KB default. What the linker checks is
-# the reservation: it refuses scratch code that would overlap the reserved 4 KB. The stack's real depth is still the
-# hand sum, with no limit at run time. Core 1's reservation (PICO_CORE1_STACK_SIZE, which defaults to this one) stays
-# its 2 KB in SCRATCH_X: core 1 never runs, and SCRATCH_X keeps room for scratch code.
+# The image runs from SRAM: the SDK's copy_to_ram binary type, whose boot copies it out of flash (flash then holds only
+# the load image and the staged ROMs). Run from flash, every instruction comes through the 16 KB XIP cache, and a
+# message's own path (the parse and the staging, the block's three nodes, the cart link's push and drain, the FIFO write
+# through the Edio and TinyUSB) runs once a message, so between isolated messages it falls out of the cache and each
+# 8-byte line comes back from the QSPI flash (quad EBh at clk_sys/3), about 90 cycles a line. On the rig an isolated
+# message's way from its UART poll to its FIFO write took about 11,200 cycles with about 90 refills from flash and
+# 3,200 with none from SRAM, its fifoWR call 91 us and 38, and stress.sh's isolated latency (average/worst, us) went
+# from 689-742/1192-1248 (four runs; a fifth held a message 12.6 ms behind a console line, as E2 can too) to
+# 588-720/1080-1128 (five), where E2's image, half the size, gave 558-653/1083-1097 from flash. It costs SRAM: the
+# code and constants sit beside the data, about 305 KiB of the 512 KiB in all where running from flash took about 200
+# (the plan's 128 KiB arena among them), which leaves about 200 KiB for a later plan's audio and E4's script heap.
+pico_set_binary_type(n8_host copy_to_ram)
+# A 4 KB main stack: all of SCRATCH_Y, which holds nothing else. The box's deepest chains, summed pessimistically from
+# -fstack-usage: the plan's load at boot (main, BuiltInPlan::load, loadPlan, its layout, a node's query_memory and its
+# settings' decode) about 2.5 KB, before the UART and USB interrupts are on; a boot through bootRom and box.cfg's save,
+# a transport wait, TinyUSB's callbacks and printf, with the UART and SOF interrupts nested on top, about 2.3 KB; a
+# block (main, BuiltInPlan::run, runBlock, rp.n8.nes's process, the link's push) about 0.6 KB. What the linker checks is
+# the reservation: it refuses scratch code that would overlap the reserved 4 KB. Every frame is held to 1 KB at build
+# time (-Wstack-usage, cmake/device-image.cmake), and the chains are still the hand sum, with no limit at run time.
+# In the PIO-USB build, which links pico_multicore (Pico-PIO-USB does), core 1's reservation (PICO_CORE1_STACK_SIZE,
+# which defaults to this one) stays its 2 KB in SCRATCH_X: core 1 never runs, and SCRATCH_X keeps room for scratch
+# code. The native build links no pico_multicore and reserves no core 1 stack.
 target_compile_definitions(n8_host PRIVATE PICO_STACK_SIZE=0x1000 PICO_CORE1_STACK_SIZE=0x800)
-# The box's product: the N8 pack's device entry (rp.n8.nes), registered as a device registers it, and the pack's
-# portable library (the Edio, its menu commands and operations) linked in.
-retroplug_product(n8-host DEVICE PACKAGES n8 TARGETS n8_host)
-target_link_libraries(n8_host PRIVATE retroplug-graph-exec)
+# No heap reserved (the SDK's .heap section, 2 KB by default): nothing in the image allocates, which the link trap
+# holds, so the reservation would be RAM no one can use. The plan's memory is its arena, a static below.
+target_compile_definitions(n8_host PRIVATE PICO_HEAP_SIZE=0)
+# The box's product: the device entries of the packages its plan names (rp.core, rp.device and rp.n8), registered as a
+# device registers them, which is what the loader holds the plan's types to at boot, and the N8 pack's portable library
+# (the Edio, its menu commands and operations) linked in; the generic box host; the plan's header and its arena.
+retroplug_product(n8-host DEVICE PACKAGES core device-io n8 TARGETS n8_host)
+target_link_libraries(n8_host PRIVATE rp-box-host retroplug-graph-exec)
+target_include_directories(n8_host PRIVATE "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/generated")
+target_compile_definitions(n8_host PRIVATE N8_HOST_ARENA_BYTES=${N8_HOST_ARENA_BYTES})
 
 # Experiment knobs, each a plain #define in main.cpp with a default: N8_MENU_TRIES (how many

-foreach(knob N8_MENU_TRIES N8_APU_LAT N8_EXP_VOL N8_TEST_HOOKS)

+# the box and what each part of a pass costs, printed after a second of quiet). The expansion volume is no knob: it is
+# rp.n8.nes's `expansionVolume` param, unity unless plan.json sets it, which the cart link writes.
+foreach(knob N8_MENU_TRIES N8_APU_LAT N8_TEST_HOOKS N8_LAT_TRACE)
     if(DEFINED ${knob})

@@ -85,12 +85,28 @@ elf=$bdir/n8_host.elf
 # --- build -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 if [ $do_build = 1 ]; then
 	echo "== build ($(basename "$bdir"), SDK $sdk)"
+	mkdir -p "$bdir"
+	# The firmware's build exports its built-in plan (plan.json) with the desktop build's retroplug-export-plan
+	# (RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR, default build/, as tools/build-box.sh reads it), handed to the configure by path. This
+	# script does not build the desktop tree: another session may be building it, and two builds of one tree at once
+	# race. It takes the exporter as that tree last built it (tools/build-box.sh and pnpm test:plugin build it; it is in
+	# no default target, so a plain desktop build does not), and the firmware's export reruns whenever the exporter,
+	# plan.json or plan.cmake changes; a package changed since the exporter was built wants the exporter built first
+	# (the box's loader refuses, at boot and in words, a blob of another format).
+	# Absolute, as CMake stores the tool's path in the build dir's cache, so the comparison below sees the same path.
+	desk=$(cd "${RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR:-$repo/build}" 2>/dev/null && pwd) \
+		|| die "no desktop build at ${RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR:-$repo/build} (RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR; ./build.sh makes build/)"
+	tool=$desk/export-plan/retroplug-export-plan
+	[ -x "$tool" ] || die "no plan exporter at $tool: build it first (cmake --build $desk --target retroplug-export-plan)"
 	if [ ! -f "$bdir/build.ninja" ]; then
-		mkdir -p "$bdir"
 		# reflect-cpp's headers from the desktop build's checkout when there is one: no clone at configure.
-		reflect=$(sed -n 's/^reflectcpp_SOURCE_DIR:STATIC=//p' "$repo/build/CMakeCache.txt" 2>/dev/null)
-		PICO_SDK_PATH=$sdk cmake -S "$here" -B "$bdir" -G Ninja $cfg ${reflect:+-DRP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR="$reflect"} \
-			>"$bdir/loop-configure.log" 2>&1 \
+		reflect=$(sed -n 's/^reflectcpp_SOURCE_DIR:STATIC=//p' "$desk/CMakeCache.txt" 2>/dev/null)
+		PICO_SDK_PATH=$sdk cmake -S "$here" -B "$bdir" -G Ninja $cfg -DRP_EXPORT_PLAN_TOOL="$tool" \
+			${reflect:+-DRP_REFLECTCPP_SOURCE_DIR="$reflect"} >"$bdir/loop-configure.log" 2>&1 \
+			|| { tail -20 "$bdir/loop-configure.log"; die "configure failed (log: $bdir/loop-configure.log)"; }
+	elif [ "$(sed -n 's/^RP_EXPORT_PLAN_TOOL:FILEPATH=//p' "$bdir/CMakeCache.txt")" != "$tool" ]; then
+		# A build dir configured before (or against another desktop build): point it at this exporter.
+		cmake -B "$bdir" -DRP_EXPORT_PLAN_TOOL="$tool" >"$bdir/loop-configure.log" 2>&1 \
 			|| { tail -20 "$bdir/loop-configure.log"; die "configure failed (log: $bdir/loop-configure.log)"; }
 	fi
 	cmake --build "$bdir" -j"$(nproc)" >"$bdir/loop-build.log" 2>&1 \
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The box's portable pieces, tested on the desktop**

`fake-tinyusb/tusb.h` and `fake-tinyusb/pico/time.h` and `FakeTinyUsb.{hpp,cpp}` are the five TinyUSB calls
`UsbCdcTransport` makes and the SDK clock, with a TX FIFO, a clock each pump moves on, scripted input and an `onPump`
hook standing in for TinyUSB's callbacks; only `retroplug-box-usb-cdc`'s compile (an object library of
`UsbCdcTransport.cpp`, on the Windows `/W4` list) sees them. `UsbCdcTransport.test.cpp` (`[usb-cdc]`, 5 cases): a
write that hands every byte then waits, flushing; the best-effort drain and the 2 s stall; an unmount mid-take; a
remount in one pump; a read's and a flush's waits. `BoxHost.test.cpp` (`[box]`): the driver's arithmetic, its carry
and bound (a 12 s wait runs 4 blocks, every frame run or counted skipped; an 11 ms stall carries whole); the staging
and its bounds; staged MIDI reaching `plan.json`'s loaded plan at its arrival's frame; the link's ring, refusals,
batching, volume and note-offs; the whole pass over the device's builds with no allocation; the box's commands getting
through a silenced `rp.device.midi-in`, a plan with none and no plan; a refused plan and a faulting node; the volume
write over a scripted transport, one section per outcome; and `plan.json`'s blob, from the tool in its own process, as
its golden, the loaded plan taking exactly what the export measured. **`golden/box-plan.hex` is a new file, not a
re-recording**: the box plan's 784-byte blob as hex, recorded once by the prototype (`RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE=1` is what
records it, and no step here sets it), placed from its text and held to its blob hash; `plan-blob.hex` is untouched.
`DeviceModeNodes.cpp` builds the box's link into the device-mode objects too, behind a C shim (`rp_devtest_box_*`,
`BoxRecord`, `BoxCounts` in `DeviceModeEntries.hpp`), where it derives the device-mode build's `CartLink` as the box's
derives the device's. `tests.cmake` includes `host.cmake` and `plan.cmake`, adds the sources and the box's plan
settings as definitions; `warnings.cmake` adds `retroplug-box-usb-cdc`.

Create `packages/native/test/device-mode/fake-tinyusb/tusb.h`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// A fake of the TinyUSB host calls the box's UsbCdcTransport makes (pico/n8-host/UsbCdcTransport.cpp), and nothing
// more: tuh_task and the CDC host's write, flush, read and free-space calls, with TinyUSB's signatures. What they do is
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The fake TinyUSB host behind UsbCdcTransport's desktop test (fake-tinyusb/tusb.h and pico/time.h declare what it
// defines): a clock in milliseconds that every tuh_task moves on, a TX FIFO that takes what fits and sends what a flush
// let go, a pump at a time, and input that arrives at the moments a test scripts. A test reaches into it between calls
// and through onPump, which runs inside every tuh_task as TinyUSB's callbacks do (the CDC unmount among them).

#include <cstdint>
#include <deque>
#include <functional>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace fakeusb {

struct Usb {
    std::uint64_t ms = 0;            // the clock
    std::uint32_t msPerPump = 1;     // what one tuh_task moves it on by
    std::uint32_t fifoSize = 256;    // the TX FIFO (CFG_TUH_CDC_TX_BUFSIZE)
    std::uint32_t fifoFree = 256;
    std::uint32_t takeLimit = 0;     // the most one tuh_cdc_write takes (0: whatever fits)
    std::uint32_t sendPerPump = 64;  // what a flushed FIFO sends in one pump (one packet)
    bool          flushed = false;   // a flush let the FIFO go, until it is empty
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> taken; // what the FIFO took, in order
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> sent;  // what left it
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> writeIdx;  // the CDC index each byte was written to
    std::deque<std::pair<std::uint64_t, std::uint8_t>> arriving;  // input, at the moment it arrives
    std::deque<std::uint8_t> input;  // arrived, not yet read
    std::uint32_t pumps = 0;
    std::uint32_t flushes = 0;
    std::function<void()> onPump;    // inside each tuh_task, after the clock and the FIFO have moved
};

// The one fake, reset by a test before it starts.
Usb& usb();
void reset();

}  // namespace fakeusb
````

````cpp
#include "FakeTinyUsb.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

#include "fake-tinyusb/pico/time.h"
#include "fake-tinyusb/tusb.h"

namespace fakeusb {

Usb& usb() {
    static Usb u;
    return u;
}

void reset() { usb() = Usb{}; }

}  // namespace fakeusb

using fakeusb::usb;

extern "C" {

void tuh_task(void) {
    auto& u = usb();
    ++u.pumps;
    u.ms += u.msPerPump;
    if (u.flushed) {
        const std::uint32_t queued = u.fifoSize - u.fifoFree;
        const std::uint32_t n = std::min(queued, u.sendPerPump);
        const auto begin = u.taken.end() - queued;
        u.sent.insert(u.sent.end(), begin, begin + n);
        u.fifoFree += n;
        if (u.fifoFree == u.fifoSize) u.flushed = false;
    }
    while (!u.arriving.empty() && u.arriving.front().first <= u.ms) {
        u.input.push_back(u.arriving.front().second);
        u.arriving.pop_front();
    }
    if (u.onPump) u.onPump();
}

std::uint32_t tuh_cdc_write_available(std::uint8_t) { return usb().fifoFree; }

std::uint32_t tuh_cdc_write(std::uint8_t idx, void const* buffer, std::uint32_t bufsize) {
    auto&         u = usb();
    std::uint32_t n = std::min(bufsize, u.fifoFree);
    if (u.takeLimit) n = std::min(n, u.takeLimit);
    const auto* bytes = static_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(buffer);
    u.taken.insert(u.taken.end(), bytes, bytes + n);
    u.writeIdx.insert(u.writeIdx.end(), n, idx);
    u.fifoFree -= n;
    return n;
}

std::uint32_t tuh_cdc_write_flush(std::uint8_t) {
    auto& u = usb();
    ++u.flushes;
    if (u.fifoFree != u.fifoSize) u.flushed = true;
    return 0;
}

std::uint32_t tuh_cdc_read(std::uint8_t, void* buffer, std::uint32_t bufsize) {
    auto&         u = usb();
    std::uint32_t n = 0;
    auto*         out = static_cast<std::uint8_t*>(buffer);
    while (n < bufsize && !u.input.empty()) {
        out[n++] = u.input.front();
        u.input.pop_front();
    }
    return n;
}

}  // extern "C"

absolute_time_t get_absolute_time(void) { return usb().ms * 1000; }
std::uint32_t   to_ms_since_boot(absolute_time_t t) { return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(t / 1000); }
````

````cpp
// The box's Edio link (pico/n8-host/UsbCdcTransport.cpp, docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 8) over a fake
// TinyUSB host (FakeTinyUsb.hpp): the rules E2 proved on the rig and by reading, held on the desktop.
//
// - A write gives the FIFO every byte, flushing as it goes, then waits for the bytes to leave, flushing until the
//   FIFO's free space is back; that wait is best effort (still queued at kDrainMs is a success), and a FIFO that takes
//   nothing for kWriteMs is a short write.
// - An unmount (the CDC unmount callback's unbind, which runs inside a pump) fails the call in flight at once: a write
//   answers what it handed over (0 once its bytes were all handed over and still queued), a read and a flush return.
//   From then every call fails after one pump, and a remount carries on nothing: the new N8 hears its first byte only
//   after the main loop binds it.
// - A read answers what has arrived once nothing more is waiting, and 0 at its timeout (one pump for a timeout of 0);
//   an input flush drops what arrives until kFlushQuietMs pass with nothing.
// - Every wait pumps the USB host and the idle hook, never a bare sleep.

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

#include "FakeTinyUsb.hpp"
#include "UsbCdcTransport.hpp"

namespace {

int gIdles = 0;
void idle() { ++gIdles; }

std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes(std::size_t n, std::uint8_t first = 0) {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> v(n);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) v[i] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(first + i);
    return v;
}

struct Rig {
    UsbCdcTransport usb{&idle};
    Rig() {
        fakeusb::reset();
        gIdles = 0;
        usb.bind(0);
    }
};

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a CDC write hands the FIFO every byte, then waits, flushing, for them to leave", "[device-mode][usb-cdc]") {
    Rig  rig;
    auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
    const auto data = bytes(300);
    CHECK(rig.usb.write(data.data(), data.size()) == 300);
    CHECK(u.taken == data);
    CHECK(u.sent == data);  // it returned once the FIFO was empty again
    CHECK(u.fifoFree == u.fifoSize);
    CHECK(u.flushes > 0);
    CHECK(gIdles == static_cast<int>(u.pumps));  // every pump ran the idle hook
}

TEST_CASE("a CDC write's drain is best effort, and a FIFO that takes nothing is a short write",
          "[device-mode][usb-cdc]") {
    SECTION("still queued at kDrainMs: a success") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        u.sendPerPump = 0;  // the bytes never leave
        const auto data = bytes(10);
        CHECK(rig.usb.write(data.data(), data.size()) == 10);
        CHECK(u.taken == data);
        CHECK(u.sent.empty());
        CHECK(u.ms >= UsbCdcTransport::kDrainMs);
        CHECK(u.ms <= UsbCdcTransport::kDrainMs + 5);
    }
    SECTION("nothing taken for kWriteMs: short") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        u.fifoFree = 0;
        u.sendPerPump = 0;
        const auto data = bytes(10);
        CHECK(rig.usb.write(data.data(), data.size()) == 0);
        CHECK(u.ms > UsbCdcTransport::kWriteMs);
        CHECK(u.ms <= UsbCdcTransport::kWriteMs + 5);
    }
    SECTION("a FIFO that takes a little at a time: each take restarts the wait") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        u.takeLimit = 8;
        u.sendPerPump = 8;
        const auto data = bytes(100);
        CHECK(rig.usb.write(data.data(), data.size()) == 100);
        CHECK(u.sent == data);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("an unmount fails the CDC call in flight at once, and every call after it", "[device-mode][usb-cdc]") {
    SECTION("while the FIFO takes the bytes: what it handed over") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        u.takeLimit = 16;
        u.sendPerPump = 0;
        u.onPump = [&] {
            if (u.pumps == 3) rig.usb.unbind();
        };
        const auto data = bytes(100);
        const std::size_t sent = rig.usb.write(data.data(), data.size());
        CHECK(sent == 32);  // two pumps' takes, then the unmount in the third
        CHECK(u.ms == 3);
        CHECK_FALSE(rig.usb.linkUp());
    }
    SECTION("while the bytes leave: 0") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        u.sendPerPump = 0;
        u.onPump = [&] {
            if (u.pumps == 4) rig.usb.unbind();
        };
        const auto data = bytes(10);
        CHECK(rig.usb.write(data.data(), data.size()) == 0);
        CHECK(u.ms == 4);
    }
    SECTION("a read and a flush return") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        u.onPump = [&] {
            if (u.pumps == 2) rig.usb.unbind();
        };
        std::uint8_t buffer[8];
        CHECK(rig.usb.read(buffer, sizeof buffer, 1000) == 0);
        CHECK(u.ms == 2);
        fakeusb::reset();
        rig.usb.bind(0);
        u.arriving.push_back({1, 0x11});  // never quiet for long: only the unmount can end the flush early
        u.onPump = [&] {
            if (u.pumps == 5) rig.usb.unbind();
        };
        rig.usb.flushInput();
        CHECK(u.ms == 5);
    }
    SECTION("after it, each call fails after one pump") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        rig.usb.unbind();
        const auto   data = bytes(4);
        std::uint8_t buffer[4];
        CHECK(rig.usb.write(data.data(), data.size()) == 0);
        CHECK(rig.usb.read(buffer, sizeof buffer, 1000) == 0);
        rig.usb.flushInput();
        CHECK(u.pumps == 3);
        CHECK(u.taken.empty());
    }
}

TEST_CASE("a remount carries on nothing: the new N8 hears its first byte once the main loop binds it",
          "[device-mode][usb-cdc]") {
    Rig          rig;
    auto&        u = fakeusb::usb();
    std::uint8_t mountedIdx = 0xFF;
    // Inside one pump, as TinyUSB can deliver them: the old N8's unmount (unbind) and the new one's CDC mount, whose
    // callback only records the index (pico/n8-host/main.cpp's tuh_cdc_mount_cb).
    u.onPump = [&] {
        if (u.pumps == 2) {
            rig.usb.unbind();
            mountedIdx = 1;
        }
    };
    std::uint8_t reply[4];
    CHECK(rig.usb.read(reply, sizeof reply, 1000) == 0);  // a reply the old N8 never gave: the call ends here
    CHECK(mountedIdx == 1);
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.usb.linkUp());
    const auto rest = bytes(6, 0x40);
    CHECK(rig.usb.write(rest.data(), rest.size()) == 0);  // what a call would carry on with goes nowhere
    CHECK(u.taken.empty());

    u.onPump = nullptr;
    rig.usb.bind(mountedIdx);  // the main loop, at its top level, before the new N8's probe
    CHECK(rig.usb.linkUp());
    const auto probe = bytes(4, 0x2A);
    CHECK(rig.usb.write(probe.data(), probe.size()) == 4);
    CHECK(u.taken == probe);
    CHECK(u.writeIdx == std::vector<std::uint8_t>(4, 1));
}

TEST_CASE("a CDC read answers what has arrived, and an input flush waits for the line to go quiet",
          "[device-mode][usb-cdc]") {
    SECTION("a read") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        u.arriving = {{3, 0xA1}, {4, 0xA2}, {40, 0xA3}};
        std::uint8_t buffer[8] = {};
        CHECK(rig.usb.read(buffer, sizeof buffer, 100) == 2);  // the two together, once nothing more is waiting
        CHECK(buffer[0] == 0xA1);
        CHECK(buffer[1] == 0xA2);
        CHECK(u.ms == 5);
        const std::uint32_t before = u.pumps;
        CHECK(rig.usb.read(buffer, sizeof buffer, 0) == 0);  // a timeout of 0: one pump
        CHECK(u.pumps == before + 1);
        CHECK(rig.usb.read(buffer, 1, 100) == 1);  // the third, when it comes
        CHECK(buffer[0] == 0xA3);
        CHECK(u.ms == 40);
        CHECK(rig.usb.read(buffer, sizeof buffer, 50) == 0);
        CHECK(u.ms > 40 + 50);
    }
    SECTION("a flush") {
        Rig  rig;
        auto& u = fakeusb::usb();
        u.arriving = {{5, 0x01}, {15, 0x02}, {30, 0x03}, {80, 0x04}};
        rig.usb.flushInput();
        CHECK(u.ms >= 30 + UsbCdcTransport::kFlushQuietMs);  // 20 ms after the last byte it dropped
        CHECK(u.ms < 80);
        std::uint8_t buffer[4] = {};
        CHECK(rig.usb.read(buffer, sizeof buffer, 100) == 1);  // what arrives after the flush is kept
        CHECK(buffer[0] == 0x04);
    }
}
````
